It is not hard to check that both quantities in \eqref{eq:CPUELLTzjVsMAlwzu} count walks of length $\ell$ in $G$ starting from the oriented edge $wz$ and ending at vertex $u$. To see that \eqref{eq:CPUELLTzjVsMAlwzu} is true, we note that the l.h.s. considers only self-avoiding walks, while the r.h.s. considers simple walks., i.e., including the self-avoiding ones.

nodes.name: Bound $\mathcal{H}_\ell$ for $\ell>1$ (7.22)
nodes.statement: Combining \eqref{eq:CPUELLTzjVsMAlwzu} with \eqref{eq:FinalBoundRroorAdj} and \Cref{claim:CEllVsCalD}, for $\ell>1$, we have \begin{align} \mathcal{H}_{\ell} & \leq c \cdot \sum\nolimits_{z \in N_G(w)} \left( \delta^{\ell-1} \cdot \sum\nolimits_{u\in V\setminus \Lambda} \left( \UpC\cdot {\UpA}^{\ell-1}_G\right)(wz,u) \cdot \left ( \UpD(u)\right )^{\darkmagenta{s}} \right )^{1/\darkmagenta{s}} \enspace. \end{align}

nodes.name: Bound $\mathcal{H}_1$ by Boundedness
nodes.statement: As far as $\mathcal{H}_1$ is concerned, note that for any edge $e\in T$, we have \begin{align} \abs{\upalpha(e)}= \frac{\uppsi(e)}{\uppsi(e)} \cdot \abs{\upalpha(e)} \leq \max_{\bar{e}, \hat{e} \in T} \left\{ \uppsi(\bar{e}) \cdot \frac{\abs{\upalpha(\hat{e})}}{\uppsi(\hat{e})} \right\} \leq c \enspace, \end{align} where the last inequality follows from the Boundedness condition of the $(\darkmagenta{s},\delta,c)$-potential function ${\Psi}$. Applying the definition of $\mathcal{H}_{\ell}$ for $\ell=1$, we get \begin{align} \mathcal{H}_1 &=\sum\nolimits_{z \in N_G(w)}\UpD(z)\cdot \abs{\upalpha(e_{z})} \leq c \cdot \sum\nolimits_{z\in N_G(w)}\UpD(z)\enspace, \end{align} where $\upalpha(e_{z})$ corresponds to the weight in $T$ for the edge $e_{z}$ that connects the root of $T$ with the copy of vertex $z$. The last inequality uses \eqref{eq:BeBoundFromPotBoundedness}.

nodes.name: Sum the bounds
nodes.statement: In light of all the above, we get \eqref{eq:Target4thrm:InflNormBound4GeneralD} by plugging \eqref{eq:FinalBoundCJLAdj} and \eqref{eq:FinalBoundCJ1Adj} into \eqref{eq:bCVsbCELL} and noting that $\mathcal{H}_0=\UpD(w)$. \Cref{thrm:InflNormBound4GeneralD} follows. \hfill $\square$.

nodes.name: Define the matrix $\mathcal{J}$ counting self-avoiding copies
nodes.statement: Recall that set $\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ consists of the self-avoiding walks of length $k$ in $G$ which do not intersect with set $\Lambda$. Let $\mathcal{J}$ be the $\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}\times \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ matrix such that, for any $P,Q\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda, k}$, the entry $\mathcal{J}(P,Q)$ is defined as follows: Let $w$ and $u$ be the starting vertices of $P$ and $Q$, respectively. If $P$ and $Q$ are not compatible, i.e., ${\rm dist}_G(u,w)< 2k$, we let $\mathcal{J}(P,Q)=0$. For $P$ and $Q$ which are compatible, we consider graph $\gext{G}{P,Q}$, the $(P,Q)$-extension of $G$, and let $T_{P,Q}=T_{\rm SAW}(\gext{G}{P,Q},w)$. We let \begin{align}\nonumber \mathcal{J}(P,Q)&= \sum\nolimits_{\ell \geq 2k}\delta^{\ell}\times \abs{ \widehat{\tt A}(u,\ell)} \enspace, \end{align} where we let set $\widehat{\tt A}(u,\ell)$ consist of all copies of vertex $u$ in $T_{P,Q}$ which correspond to self-avoiding walks of length $\ell$ in $\gext{G}{P,Q}$.
nodes.statement_short: Define the matrix $\mathcal{J}$ counting self-avoiding copies

nodes.name: State Lemma 10.2
nodes.statement: \begin{lemma} We have $\abs{\applegreen{{\mathcal{L}}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G,k}} \leq \mathcal{J}$, where the inequality is entry-wise. \end{lemma} The proof of \Cref{lemma:eq:CLVsCJEntrywise} appears in \Cref{sec:lemma:eq:CLVsCJEntrywise}. As per standard notation, $\abs{\applegreen{{\mathcal{L}}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G,k}}$ in \Cref{lemma:eq:CLVsCJEntrywise} corresponds to the matrix having entries $\abs{\applegreen{{\mathcal{L}}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G,k}(P,Q)}$.

nodes.name: Proposition 9.2 and Lemma 10.2 give $\|\mathcal{I}\|_2\le...
nodes.statement:
\Cref{proposition:CINorm2VsCLNorm2} implies that there are constants $c_1,c_2>0$ such that  egin{align} 
orm{ {\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,	au}_G}{2} &\leq c_1+ c_2 \cdot 
orm{\abs{\applegreen{{\mathcal{L}}}^{\Lambda,	au}_{G,k}}}{2} \ \leq \ c_1+ c_2 \cdot 
orm{ \mathcal{J}}{2} \enspace. \end{align} The second inequality follows from \Cref{lemma:eq:CLVsCJEntrywise} and the observation that $\abs{\applegreen{{\mathcal{L}}}^{\Lambda,	au}_{G,k}}$ and $\mathcal{J}$ have non-negative entries.

nodes.name: State Proposition 10.3
nodes.statement:
egin{proposition} We have  egin{align} 
orm{ \mathcal{J}}{2} &\leq \sum 
olimits_{\ell\geq k} \delta^{\ell+k} \cdot 
orm{ ( \cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k} )^{\ell}}{2} \enspace. \end{align} \end{proposition} The proof of \Cref{prop:CJVskNBM} appears in \Cref{sec:prop:CJVskNBM}.

nodes.name: Plug in and set constants
nodes.statement: \Cref{thrm:L2InflRedux2KNBTM} follows by plugging \eqref{eq:thrm:DomOfInflB} into \eqref{eq:IVsJ2Norm} and setting $C_1=c_1$ and $C_2=c_2\cdot \delta^{k}$. \hfill $\square$

nodes.name: Non-compatible pairs: both sides vanish
nodes.statement: When there is no danger of confusion, in what follows we abbreviate matrix $\applegreen{{\mathcal{L}}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G,k}$ to $\rosegold{{\mathcal{L}}}$. Let $P,Q \in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda, k}$, while let $w$ and $u$ be their starting vertices, respectively. For non-compatible $P, Q$, the definitions of matrices $\rosegold{{\mathcal{L}}}$ and $ \mathcal{J}$ imply that $\rosegold{{\mathcal{L}}}(P,Q)= \mathcal{J}(P,Q)=0$.

nodes.name: Compatible pairs: write $\mathcal{L}(P,Q)$ as an influence of the...
nodes.statement: We consider compatible $P$ and $Q$. It suffices to show that $\abs{\rosegold{{\mathcal{L}}}(P,Q)} \leq \mathcal{J}(P,Q)$. We let $\upzeta^{P,Q}$ be the $\{P,Q\}$-extension of $\mu^{\Lambda,\tau}_G$, while let ${\mathcal{I}}^{P,Q}$ be the influence matrix induced by $\upzeta^{P,Q}$. Recall from \eqref{def:EdgeInflMatrixEquivalent} that \begin{align} \rosegold{{\mathcal{L}}}(P, Q)={\mathcal{I}}^{P,Q}(w,u)\enspace, \end{align} where, as mentioned above, $w$ and $u$ are the starting vertices of $P$ and $Q$, respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Compatible pairs: write $\mathcal{L}(P,Q)$ as an influence of the extension

nodes.name: Expand the influence over $T_{\rm SAW}$ paths
nodes.statement:
Let $T_{P,Q}=T_{m SAW}(\gext{G}{P,Q}, w)$. Also, let $\{\upalpha(e)\}$ be the collection of weights over the edges of $T_{P,Q}$ we obtain as described in \eqref{def:OfInfluenceWeights} with respect to the Gibbs distribution $\upzeta^{P,Q}$. We have  egin{align} {\mathcal{I}}^{P,Q}(w,u)&=\sum
olimits_{\ell \geq 2k}\sum
olimits_{W\in T_{P,Q} : \abs{W}=\ell} \prod
olimits_{e\in W} \upalpha(e)\enspace, \end{align} where $W$ varies over the paths of length $\ell$ in $T_{P,Q}$ from the root to the copies of vertex $u$ corresponding to self-avoiding walks in $\gext{G}{P,Q}$. Any copies of $u$ in $T_{P,Q}$ that do not correspond to self-avoiding walk have a pinning. The influence of the root to vertices with pinning is zero.
nodes.statement_short: Expand the influence over $T_{\rm SAW}$ paths

nodes.name: Each path weight is at most $\delta^\ell$
nodes.statement_short: Each path weight is at most $\delta^\ell$

nodes.name: Entrywise bound holds
nodes.statement: The above proves that indeed $\abs{\rosegold{{\mathcal{L}}}(P,Q)} \leq \mathcal{J}(P,Q)$ for $P$ and $Q$ which are compatible. \Cref{lemma:eq:CLVsCJEntrywise} follows. \hfill $\square$

nodes.name: Entrywise bound (10.10) of $\mathcal{J}$ by...
nodes.statement:
First, we show that the following entry-wise inequality  egin{align} \mathcal{J} \leq \sum
olimits_{\ell\geq k}\delta^{\ell+k}\cdot ( ( \cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k} )^{\ell}\cdot \UpR )_{\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}}\enspace, \end{align} where $\UpR$ is the involution defined in \eqref{def:OfInvolutation}, while $\left( ( \cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k} )^{\ell}\cdot \UpR ight)_{\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}}$ is the principal submatrix of $( \cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k} )^{\ell}\cdot \UpR$ induced by the elements in $\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$. Consider $P,Q\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$, which are compatible. Let $w$ and $u$ be the starting vertices of $P$ and $Q$, respectively. Consider $\gext{G}{P,Q}$, the $(P,Q)$-extension of graph $G$ and let $T_{P,Q}=T_{m SAW}(\gext{G}{P,Q},w)$. From the definition of matrix $\mathcal{J}$, we have  egin{align} \mathcal{J}(P,Q)&=\sum
olimits_{\ell\geq 2k}\delta^{\ell}\cdot \abs{\widehat{	t A}(u,\ell)} \enspace, \end{align} where recall that $\widehat{	t A}(u,\ell)$ is the set of copies of vertex $u$ in $T_{P,Q}$ which correspond to self-avoiding walks of length $\ell$ in $\gext{G}{P,Q}$. The vertex $u$ is the starting vertex of $Q$. Note that the compatibility assumption for $P$ and $Q$ implies ${m dist}_{G}(w,u)\geq 2k$. Hence the copies of $u$ in $T$ are at distance $\geq 2k$ from the root. For $\ell\geq 2k$, we obtain a bound on $\abs{\widehat{	t A}(u,\ell)}$ in terms of the $k$-non-backtracking matrix $\cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k}$. W.l.o.g. let $P=v_0, \ldots, v_{k}$ and $Q=x_0,\ldots, x_{k}$. The cardinality of set $\widehat{	t A}(u,\ell)$ is equal to the number of self-avoiding walks $R=z_0,\ldots, z_{\ell}$ in $\gext{G}{P,Q}$, satisfying the following condition: for $0\leq i \leq k$, we have  egin{itemize} \item $z_{i}$ is a copy of vertex $v_{i}$ and $z_{\ell-{i}}$ is a copy of $x_{i}$. \end{itemize} Recall that the additional vertices that $\gext{G}{P,Q}$ has compared to $G$ are split-vertices, each of which is of degree $1$. No split-vertex can be a part of a self-avoiding walk from $w$ to $u$. Hence, every self-avoiding walk $R$ in $\gext{G}{P,Q}$ that satisfies the above condition also appears in $G$. Furthermore, since every self-avoiding walk of length $\ell$ from $w$ to $u$ in $G$ can also be considered as a $k$-non-backtracking walk of length $\ell-k$ from $P$ to $Q^{-1}$, we conclude that  egin{align}
onumber \abs{\widehat{	t A}(u,\ell)} &\leq ( \cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k} )^{\ell-k}(P,Q^{-1}) = ( ( \cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^{\ell-k} \cdot \UpR ) (P,Q) \enspace. \end{align} Walk $Q^{-1}$ corresponds to $Q$ reversed, i.e., $Q^{-1}=x_{k},x_{k-1}, \ldots, x_0$. Plugging the above inequality into \eqref{eq:RedefInfmatrixBP-Q}, we get that \eqref{eq:Final4prop:CJVskNBM} is true for compatible walks $P$ and $Q$. For non-compatible $P,Q$, the definition of $\mathcal{J}$ specifies that $\mathcal{J}(P,Q)=0$. This implies that \eqref{eq:Final4prop:CJVskNBM} is true even for non-compatible $P$ and $Q$ since we always have $( ( \cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^{\ell-k} \cdot \UpR ) (P,Q)\geq 0$. All the above establish that \eqref{eq:Final4prop:CJVskNBM} is true.

nodes.name: Compatible pairs: recall the definition of $\mathcal{J}$
nodes.statement: Consider $P,Q\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$, which are compatible. Let $w$ and $u$ be the starting vertices of $P$ and $Q$, respectively. Consider $\gext{G}{P,Q}$, the $(P,Q)$-extension of graph $G$ and let $T_{P,Q}=T_{\rm SAW}(\gext{G}{P,Q},w)$. From the definition of matrix $\mathcal{J}$, we have \begin{align} \mathcal{J}(P,Q)&=\sum\nolimits_{\ell\geq 2k}\delta^{\ell}\cdot \abs{\widehat{\tt A}(u,\ell)} \enspace, \end{align} where recall that $\widehat{\tt A}(u,\ell)$ is the set of copies of vertex $u$ in $T_{P,Q}$ which correspond to self-avoiding walks of length $\ell$ in $\gext{G}{P,Q}$. The vertex $u$ is the starting vertex of $Q$. Note that the compatibility assumption for $P$ and $Q$ implies ${\rm dist}_{G}(w,u)\geq 2k$. Hence the copies of $u$ in $T$ are at distance $\geq 2k$ from the root.
nodes.statement_short: Compatible pairs: recall the definition of $\mathcal{J}$

nodes.name: Describe $\widehat{\tt A}(u,\ell)$ as counted self-avoiding walks
nodes.statement: For $\ell\geq 2k$, we obtain a bound on $\abs{\widehat{\tt A}(u,\ell)}$ in terms of the $k$-non-backtracking matrix $\cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k}$. W.l.o.g. let $P=v_0, \ldots, v_{k}$ and $Q=x_0,\ldots, x_{k}$. The cardinality of set $\widehat{\tt A}(u,\ell)$ is equal to the number of self-avoiding walks $R=z_0,\ldots, z_{\ell}$ in $\gext{G}{P,Q}$, satisfying the following condition: for $0\leq i \leq k$, we have \begin{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Describe $\widehat{\tt A}(u,\ell)$ as counted self-avoiding walks

nodes.name: Endpoint condition on the walks
nodes.statement: $z_{i}$ is a copy of vertex $v_{i}$ and $z_{\ell-{i}}$ is a copy of $x_{i}$. \end{itemize}

nodes.name: Walks avoid split-vertices, so they are counted by...
nodes.statement: Recall that the additional vertices that $\gext{G}{P,Q}$ has compared to $G$ are split-vertices, each of which is of degree $1$. No split-vertex can be a part of a self-avoiding walk from $w$ to $u$. Hence, every self-avoiding walk $R$ in $\gext{G}{P,Q}$ that satisfies the above condition also appears in $G$. Furthermore, since every self-avoiding walk of length $\ell$ from $w$ to $u$ in $G$ can also be considered as a $k$-non-backtracking walk of length $\ell-k$ from $P$ to $Q^{-1}$, we conclude that \begin{align}\nonumber \abs{\widehat{\tt A}(u,\ell)} &\leq ( \cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k} )^{\ell-k}(P,Q^{-1}) = ( ( \cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^{\ell-k} \cdot \UpR ) (P,Q) \enspace. \end{align} Walk $Q^{-1}$ corresponds to $Q$ reversed, i.e., $Q^{-1}=x_{k},x_{k-1}, \ldots, x_0$. Plugging the above inequality into \eqref{eq:RedefInfmatrixBP-Q}, we get that \eqref{eq:Final4prop:CJVskNBM} is true for compatible walks $P$ and $Q$.
nodes.statement_short: Walks avoid split-vertices, so they are counted by $H^{\ell-k}_{G,k}(P,Q^{-1})$

nodes.name: Non-compatible pairs are trivial
nodes.statement: For non-compatible $P,Q$, the definition of $\mathcal{J}$ specifies that $\mathcal{J}(P,Q)=0$. This implies that \eqref{eq:Final4prop:CJVskNBM} is true even for non-compatible $P$ and $Q$ since we always have $( ( \cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^{\ell-k} \cdot \UpR ) (P,Q)\geq 0$.

nodes.name: Entrywise bound (10.10) holds
nodes.statement: All the above establish that \eqref{eq:Final4prop:CJVskNBM} is true.

nodes.name: Triangle inequality, interlacing and $\|R\|_2=1$
nodes.statement:
Furthermore, \eqref{eq:Final4prop:CJVskNBM}, the fact that both $\mathcal{J}$ and $\left( \cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k}ight)^{\ell-k}\cdot \UpR$ have non-negative entries and the triangle inequality imply  egin{align}
onumber 
orm{ \mathcal{J}}{2} & \leq \sum
olimits_{\ell\geq k}\delta^{\ell+k}\cdot 
orm{ (( \cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^{\ell} \cdot \UpR )_{\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda, k}}}2 \leq \sum
olimits_{\ell\geq k}\delta^{\ell+k}\cdot 
orm{ ( \cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^{\ell} \cdot \UpR }{2} \leq \sum
olimits_{\ell\geq k}\delta^{\ell+k}\cdot 
orm{ ( \cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^{\ell} }{2} \enspace. 
onumber \end{align} The second inequality follows from Cauchy’s interlacing theorem. Note that matrix $(\cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^{\ell} \cdot \UpR$ is symmetric due to \eqref{eq:DefPTInvarianceFormalB}. The third inequality follows since $
orm{ ( \cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^{\ell} \cdot \UpR }{2}\leq 
orm{ ( \cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^{\ell}}{2}\cdot 
orm{ \UpR }{2}$ while, for the involutionary matrix $\UpR$, we have $
orm{ \UpR}{2}=1$. \Cref{prop:CJVskNBM} follows. \hfill $\square$

nodes.name: Define entrywise powers and the matrices $\mathcal{D}_\ell$
nodes.statement:
For a vector ${ f v}\in \mathbb{R}^{N}_{\geq 0}$, and $r \in \mathbb{R}$, we let vector ${ f v}^{r}$ be such that ${ f v}^{r}(i)=({ f v}(i))^{r}$, for $1\leq i \leq N$. Also, when there is no danger of confusion, we abbreviate $\applegreen{{\mathcal{L}}}^{\Lambda,	au}_{G,k}$ to $osegold{{\mathcal{L}}}$. For integer $\ell\geq 2k$, we let $\mathcal{D}_{\ell}$ be the $\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}	imes \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ matrix such that for $P,Q \in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$, the entry $\mathcal{D}_{\ell}(P,Q)$ is defined as follows: Let $w$ and $u$ be the starting vertices of $P$ and $Q$, respectively. Assume, first, that $P$ and $Q$ are compatible, i.e., ${m dist}_G(w,u)\geq 2k$. Let $\gext{G}{P,Q}$ and $\upzeta^{P,Q}$ be the $\{P,Q\}$-extensions of $G$ and $\mu^{\Lambda,	au}_G$, respectively. Also, let $\cadmiumgreen{T_{P,Q}}=T_{m SAW}(G_{P,Q}, w)$ and the weights $\{ \upalpha_{P,Q}(e)\}$ are obtained as specified in \eqref{def:OfInfluenceWeights} with respect to $\upzeta^{P,Q}$. We let  egin{align}
onumber \mathcal{D}_{\ell}(P, Q) &=\sum
olimits_{W\in \cadmiumgreen{T_{P,Q}}: \abs{W}=\ell} \prod
olimits_{e\in W} \abs{\upalpha_{P,Q}(e)} \enspace, \end{align} where $W$ varies over all the paths of length $\ell$ from the root to the copies of $u$ in $\cadmiumgreen{T_{P,Q}}$ that correspond to self-avoiding walks. For non-compatible walks $P$ and $Q$, we let $\mathcal{D}_{\ell}(P, Q) =0$.
nodes.statement_short: Define entrywise powers and the matrices $\mathcal{D}_\ell$

nodes.name: Reduce to the bound (12.1) on $\|\mathcal{D}_\ell\|_{2s}$
Define the walk-copy counting matrices $Z^{(\ell)}$
nodes.statement: Before showing that \eqref{eq:Target4thrm:InfNormBoundHConjLL} is true, we introduce a few concepts and establish some useful technical results. For $\ell\geq 2k$, we let $\red{\UpZ}^{(\ell)}$ be the $\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}\times \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ matrix such that for $P,Q \in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$, the entry $\red{\UpZ}^{(\ell)}(P,Q)$ is defined as follows: Let $w$ and $u$ be the starting vertices of $P$ and $Q$, respectively. For $P$ and $Q$ which are compatible, we consider $\byzantine{\overline{T}}=T_{\rm SAW}(\gext{G}{P}, w)$ and let \begin{align}\nonumber \red{\UpZ}^{(\ell)}(P, Q) &=\# \textrm{copies of walk $Q$ in $\byzantine{\overline{T}}$ which is at distance $\ell$ from the root} \enspace. \end{align} For vertex $x$ in $\byzantine{\overline{T}}$, which is connected to the root of the tree with path $W=x_0, \ldots, x_{\ell}$, i.e., $x_0$ is the root and $x_{\ell}$ is $x$; we say that $x$ is a copy of walk $Q=z_0,\ldots, z_{k}$, if $x_{\ell-i}$ is a copy of $z_{i}$, for all $i=0,\ldots, k$. For non-compatible $P$ and $Q$, we have $\red{\UpZ}^{(\ell)}(P, Q) =0$.

nodes.name: Define the vectors $f$, $g$, $k$
nodes.statement: For integer $\ell\geq 2k$ and $\iris{{\bf q}} \in \mathbb{R}^{\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}}_{\geq 0}$, let vectors $\upf_{\iris{{\bf q}}, \ell},\upg_{\iris{{\bf q}}, \ell}, \upk_{\iris{{\bf q}}, \ell} \in \mathbb{R}^{\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}}_{\geq 0}$ be defined as follows: We let \begin{align} \upf_{\iris{{\bf q}}, \ell}=\mathcal{D}_{\ell}\cdot \iris{{\bf q}} \enspace. \end{align} We also let \begin{align} \upg_{\iris{{\bf q}}, \ell} &= \left( {\textstyle \frac{1-\varepsilon/2}{\uprho}} \right)^{\ell/\darkmagenta{s}} \cdot \left( \red{\UpZ}^{(\ell)}\cdot \iris{{\bf q}}^{\darkmagenta{s}}\right)^{1/\darkmagenta{s}} \enspace. \end{align} Similarly, we let \begin{align} \upk_{\iris{{\bf q}}, \ell}&= {\textstyle \left(\frac{1-\varepsilon/2}{\uprho}\right)^{\ell/\darkmagenta{s}} } \cdot \left( ( ( \cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^{\ell-k}\cdot \UpR)_{\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}} \cdot \iris{{\bf q}}^{\darkmagenta{s}}\right)^{1/\darkmagenta{s}} \enspace, \end{align} where $\UpR$ is the $\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{k}\times \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{k}$ involutionary matrix defined in \eqref{def:OfInvolutation}. Also, $(( \cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^{{\ell-k}}\cdot \UpR)_{\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}}$ corresponds to the principle submatrix of $( \cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^{\ell-k}\cdot \UpR$ induced by the elements in $\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda, k}\subseteq \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{k}$.

nodes.name: State Proposition 12.1
nodes.statement: \begin{proposition} For $k\geq 1$, there exists a constant $\widehat{c}_0\geq 1$ such that, for any $\ell\geq 2k$ and any $\iris{{\bf q}} \in \mathbb{R}^{\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}}_{\geq 0}$ \begin{align} \upf^{\darkmagenta{s}}_{\iris{{\bf q}}, \ell} &\leq \widehat{c}_0 \cdot \upg^{\darkmagenta{s}}_{\iris{{\bf q}}, \ell} \enspace, \end{align} where the inequality between the two vectors is entry-wise. \end{proposition} The proof of \Cref{thrm:HC-VEntryBound} appears in \Cref{sec:thrm:HC-VEntryBound}.

nodes.name: Entrywise chain $0\le f\le\widehat c_0g\le\widehat c_0k$
nodes.statement: Letting ${\bf 0}\in \mathbb{R}^{\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}}$ be the all-zeros vector, for any $\iris{{\bf q}} \in \mathbb{R}^{\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}}_{\geq 0}$, for any $\ell\geq 2k$, we have \begin{align} {\bf 0}\leq \upf_{\iris{{\bf q}}, \ell} \leq \widehat{c}_0\cdot \upg_{\iris{{\bf q}}, \ell} \leq \widehat{c}_0\cdot \upk_{\iris{{\bf q}}, \ell}\enspace, \end{align} where the above inequalities are entry-wise, while $\widehat{c}_0$ is from \Cref{thrm:HC-VEntryBound}. To see why \eqref{eq:GKVecDom} is true, note the following: The first inequality implies that the entries of $f_{\iris{{\bf q}},\ell}$, which is defined in \eqref{eq:DefOfFvec}, are non-negative, which is true since both $\mathcal{D}_{\ell}$ and $\iris{{\bf q}}$ have non-negative entries. The second inequality follows from the fact that the entries of $\upg_{\iris{{\bf q}},\ell}$ are non-negative and \Cref{thrm:HC-VEntryBound}. The third inequality follows from the observation that each entry $\red{\UpZ}^{(\ell)}(P, Q)$ is upper bounded by the number of $k$-non-backtracking walks of length $\ell-k$ from $P$ to $Q$.

nodes.name: Pick the norm-attaining $q^\star$ and bound...
nodes.statement_short: Pick the norm-attaining $q^\star$ and bound $\|\mathcal{D}_\ell\|_{2s}$ by $\|k^\star_\ell\|_{2s}$

nodes.name: Bound $\|k^\star\|$ via symmetry of $H^{\ell-k}R$ and interlacing
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\|k^\star\|$ via symmetry of $H^{\ell-k}R$ and interlacing

nodes.name: Combine and set $\widehat c$
nodes.statement: We get \eqref{eq:Target4thrm:InfNormBoundHConjLL} by plugging \eqref{eq:VevKStarNormBound} into \eqref{eq:KSNorm4L1} and setting $\widehat{c}=\widehat{c}_0\cdot \left(\frac{1-\varepsilon/2}{\uprho}\right)^{k/\darkmagenta{s}}$. \Cref{thrm:InfNormBoundHConj} follows. \hfill $\square$

nodes.name: Define $\mathcal{C}_\ell$ using $P$-extension weights
Define $z_{q,\ell}$ and state Claim 12.2
nodes.statement: For $\iris{{\bf q}} \in \mathbb{R}^{\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}}_{\geq 0}$, let \begin{align} \upz_{\iris{{\bf q}},\ell} &= {\mathcal{C}}_{\ell} \cdot \iris{{\bf q}} \enspace. \end{align} \begin{claim} There exists fixed constant $\widehat{c}_1>0$ such that for any $\iris{{\bf q}} \in \mathbb{R}^{\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}}_{\geq 0}$, we have \begin{align} \upf^{\darkmagenta{s}}_{\iris{{\bf q}}, \ell} \leq \widehat{c}_1\cdot (1+\varepsilon/3)^{\ell} \cdot \upz^{\darkmagenta{s}}_{\iris{{\bf q}},\ell} \enspace, \end{align} where the inequality between the two vectors is entry-wise. \end{claim}

nodes.name: Reduce to (12.13)
nodes.statement: In light of \Cref{claim:CQLVsCKL}, \Cref{thrm:HC-VEntryBound} follows by showing that there exists constant $\widehat{c}_2>0$ such that, for any $\ell\geq 2k$ and any $P\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$, we have \begin{align} \upz^{\darkmagenta{s}}_{\iris{{\bf q}},\ell}(P) &\leq \widehat{c}_2 \cdot (1-\varepsilon/3)^{\ell} \cdot \upg^{\darkmagenta{s}}_{\iris{{\bf q}}, \ell}(P) \enspace. \end{align} Specifically, we get \eqref{eq:thrm:HC-VEntryBoundBB} by plugging \eqref{eq:Target4thrm:InfNormBoundHConj} into \eqref{eq:CQLVsCKL} and setting $\widehat{c}_0=\widehat{c}_1\cdot \widehat{c}_2$. It remains to show that \eqref{eq:Target4thrm:InfNormBoundHConj} is true.

nodes.name: Fix $\ell$, $q$, $P$
nodes.statement: The high-level approach to obtain \eqref{eq:Target4thrm:InfNormBoundHConj} is not too different from that we use to prove \Cref{thrm:InflNormBound4GeneralD}. For what follows, we fix $\ell\geq 2k$ and vector $\iris{{\bf q}}\in \mathbb{R}^{\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}}_{\geq 0}$. Also, fix $P \in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ while let $w$ be the starting vertices of $P$. \begin{claim} For $\ell\geq 2k$ and any path $W=e_1, \ldots, e_{\ell}$ in $\byzantine{\overline{T}}=T_{\rm SAW}(\gext{G}{P}, w)$ such that $\prod^{\ell-k}_{i=1} \abs{\upalpha_{P}(e_{i})} \neq 0$, we have \begin{align} \nonumber \prod^{\ell-k}_{i=1} \abs{\upalpha_{P}(e_{i})} &=\uppsi(e_{\ell-k}) \cdot \frac{\abs{\upalpha_{P}(e_1)}}{\uppsi(e_1)} \cdot \prod^{\ell-k}_{i=2}\frac{\uppsi(e_{i-1})}{\uppsi(e_{i})} \cdot \abs{\upalpha_{P}(e_{i})} \enspace, \end{align} where $\uppsi(e)=\chi(\upalpha_{P}(e))$ and $\chi={\Psi}'$. \end{claim} \Cref{claim:AddPotential} is very similar to \Cref{claim:AddPotentialA}. For this reason, we omit its proof.

nodes.name: Define the recursion $\mathcal{R}^{(\ell)}_v$ on $\overline T$
nodes.statement:
Recall that we fix $\iris{{ f q}} \in \mathbb{R}^{\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}}_{\geq 0}$. For each vertex $v$ at level $h$ of $ yzantine{\overline{T}}=T_{m SAW}(\gext{G}{P}, w)$, where $0\leq h\leq \ell$, we let ${{\mathcal{R}}}^{(\ell)}_{v}$ be defined as follows: For $h=\ell$, we let  egin{align} {{\mathcal{R}}}^{(\ell)}_{v} &= \sum
olimits_{Q\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}: P, Q 	extrm{ compatible}} \iris{{ f q}}(Q) \cdot \mathds{1}\{v \in {	t A}(Q, \ell) \}\enspace. \end{align} For $\ell-k \leq h \leq \ell-1$, letting $v_1,\ldots, v_{d}$ be the children of $v$, we let  egin{align} {{\mathcal{R}}}^{(\ell)}_{v} &= \sum
olimits_{v_i} {{\mathcal{R}}}^{(\ell)}_{v_i}\enspace. \end{align} For a vertex $v$ at level $0<h<\ell-k$ of the tree $ yzantine{\overline{T}}$, we have  egin{align} {{\mathcal{R}}}^{(\ell)}_{v} & = \uppsi(b_{v}) \cdot \sum
olimits_{i}  rac{\abs{\upalpha_{P}(b_{i})}}{\uppsi(b_{i})} \cdot {{\mathcal{R}}}^{(\ell)}_{v_{i}}\enspace, \end{align} where $b_{i}$ is the edge that connects $v$ to its child $v_{i}$ and edge $b_{v}$ connects $v$ to its parent in tree $ yzantine{\overline{T}}$. Finally, for $h=0$, i.e., vertex $v$ is identical to the root of $ yzantine{\overline{T}}$, we let  egin{align} {{\mathcal{R}}}^{(\ell)}_v={{\mathcal{R}}}^{(\ell)}_{m root} &= \max_{e_a,e_b\in  yzantine{\overline{T}}} \left\{ \uppsi(e_a) \cdot  rac{ \abs{\upalpha_{P}(e_b)}}{\uppsi(e_b)} ight\} \cdot {{\mathcal{R}}}^{(\ell)}_{\pi} \enspace, \end{align} where vertex $\pi$ is the single child of the root of $ yzantine{\overline{T}}$.

nodes.name: State Claim 12.4 (proof omitted)
nodes.statement: \begin{claim} We have $\upz_{\iris{{\bf q}},\ell}(P)\leq {{\mathcal{R}}}^{(\ell)}_{\rm root}$. \end{claim} The proof of \Cref{claim:ZvecQLVsCalRV} is tedious but very similar to that of \Cref{claim:CEllVsCalD} in the proof of \Cref{thrm:InflNormBound4GeneralD}. For this reason we omit it.

nodes.name: Hölder near the leaves, Contraction above level $\ell-k$
nodes.statement_short: Hölder near the leaves, Contraction above level $\ell-k$

nodes.name: Bound the root child's value by $g^s_{q,\ell}(P)$
nodes.statement: For the single child of the root of $\byzantine{\overline{T}}$, vertex $\pi$, the above implies \begin{align} \left( {{\mathcal{R}}}^{(\ell)}_{\pi} \right)^{\darkmagenta{s}} &\leq {\Delta}^{k\cdot(\darkmagenta{s}-1)} \cdot \delta^{\ell-k-1}\cdot\sum\nolimits_{Q \in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}:P,Q \textrm{ compatible}} \iris{{\bf q}}^{\darkmagenta{s}}(Q) \cdot \abs{{\tt A}(Q,\ell)} \\ & = {\Delta}^{k\cdot(\darkmagenta{s}-1)} \cdot \left( {\textstyle \frac{1-\varepsilon}{\uprho} }\right)^{\ell-k-1 }\cdot ( \red{\UpZ}^{(\ell)} \cdot \iris{{\bf q}}^{\darkmagenta{s}} ) (P) \\ & \leq \left( {\textstyle \frac{1-\varepsilon}{\uprho} }\right)^{-k-1}\cdot {\Delta}^{k\cdot(\darkmagenta{s}-1)} \cdot (1-\varepsilon/3)^{\ell}\cdot \upg^{\darkmagenta{s}}_{\iris{{\bf q}}, \ell}(P) \enspace. \end{align} For \eqref{eq:AQLVSSubtree} we use the observation that since the root of $\byzantine{\overline{T}}$ has only one child, i.e., vertex $\pi$, and $\ell\geq 2k$, we have ${\tt A}(Q,\ell)\cap \byzantine{\overline{T}}_{\pi}={\tt A}(Q,\ell)$. For \eqref{eq:cQc2SBound} we use the definition of matrix $\red{\UpZ}^{(\ell)}$ and recall that $\delta=\frac{1-\varepsilon}{\uprho}$. The last inequality follows from the definition of $\upg_{\iris{{\bf q}}, \ell}$ in \eqref{eq:DefOfGvec}.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the root child's value by $g^s_{q,\ell}(P)$

nodes.name: Boundedness handles the root
nodes.statement: The boundedness property of the $(\darkmagenta{s},\delta,c)$-potential and \eqref{eq:RecurRUZRoot} imply \begin{align} \left( {{\mathcal{R}}}^{(\ell)}_{\rm root}\right)^{\darkmagenta{s}} &\leq c^{\darkmagenta{s}} \cdot \left( {{\mathcal{R}}}^{(\ell)}_{\pi}\right)^{\darkmagenta{s}} \leq c^{\darkmagenta{s}} \left( {\textstyle \frac{1-\varepsilon}{\uprho} }\right)^{-k-1 } \cdot {\Delta}^{k\cdot(\darkmagenta{s}-1)} \cdot (1-\varepsilon/3)^{\ell}\cdot \upg^{\darkmagenta{s}}_{\iris{{\bf q}}, \ell}(P)\enspace, \end{align} where for the second equality, we use \eqref{eq:FinalIineqWithVegG}.

nodes.name: Combine with Claim 12.4 and set $\widehat c_2$
nodes.statement: We get \eqref{eq:Target4thrm:InfNormBoundHConj} by combining \eqref{eq:CQRootVsCRcBoundedness} and \Cref{claim:ZvecQLVsCalRV} while setting $\widehat{c}_2=c^{\darkmagenta{s}}\cdot {\Delta}^{k\cdot(\darkmagenta{s}-1)}\cdot \left( {\textstyle \frac{1-\varepsilon}{\uprho} }\right)^{-k-1}$. All the above conclude the proof of \Cref{thrm:HC-VEntryBound}. \hfill $\square$
nodes.statement_short: Combine with Claim 12.4 and set $\widehat c_2$

nodes.name: Identify the trees and state Claim 13.5
nodes.statement: We use \Cref{lemma:Subtree4TSawU} and identify $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}=T_{\rm SAW}(\gext{G}{P}, u)$ as a subtree of $\applegreen{T}=T_{\rm SAW}(G,u)$. Recall that the edge-weights $\{ \upalpha(e)\}$ in $\applegreen{T}$ arise from $\mu^{M,\sigma}_{\applegreen{T}}$. Also, the edge-weights $\{\upalpha_{P}(e)\}$ in $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ arise from $\mu^{L,\eta}_{\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}}$. Having identified $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ as a subtree of $\applegreen{T}$, we endow $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ with the edge-weights $\{ \upalpha(e)\}_{e\in \overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}}$. Hence now we have two sets of weights for $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$. Also, recall that set $\magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$ consists of each vertex in $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ which is either a copy of vertex $v\in P$, or a copy of a split-vertex in $\cadmiumgreen{\UpS}_{P}$. We start with the following claim. \begin{claim} For any edge $f$ in $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}=T_{\rm SAW}(\gext{G}{P},u)$, at distance $\ell >10$ from $\magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$, if $\upalpha(f)=0$, then $\upalpha_{P}(f)=0$. \end{claim}
nodes.statement_short: Identify the trees and state Claim 13.5

nodes.name: Zero-weight edges are handled by Claim 13.5
nodes.statement: \Cref{claim:AlphaPZero} implies that \eqref{eq:prop:StableSSM} is true for any edge $f$ in $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ at distance $\ell>10$ from $\magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$ such that $\upalpha(f)=0$. For the rest of the proof, we consider edge $f$ in $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ such that $\upalpha(f)\neq 0$ which is at distance $\ell \geq \ell_0$ from $\magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$, where the quantity $\ell_0>10$ is specified later in the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Zero-weight edges are handled by Claim 13.5

nodes.name: Far from $\overline{\tt A}_P$, $v$ has the same children in both trees
nodes.statement: Let edge $f=\{v,x\}$ while w.l.o.g. assume that $v$ is a child of $x$. Also, let $v_1, \ldots, v_d$ be the children of $v$ in $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$. We take $f$ at distance $\ell>10$ from $\magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$. This implies that vertex $v$ has the same set of children in both trees $\applegreen{T}$ and $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$. If $v$ had children in $\applegreen{T}$ which are not in $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$, then according to \Cref{lemma:Subtree4TSawU}, we would have had $v\in \byzantine{{\tt A}}_{P}$. But since $v\in \overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$, \Cref{lemma:BoundaryTVsBoundaryTPFromU} (statement \ref{stat:B-lemma:BoundaryTVsBoundaryTPFromU}) implies that $v\in \byzantine{{\tt A}}_{P}\cap \overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}=\magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$. This cannot happen since we assume that $f$ is at distance at least $10$ from $\magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$. Hence, $v$ indeed has the same set of children in both trees $\applegreen{T}$ and $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Far from $\overline{\tt A}_P$, $v$ has the same children in both trees

nodes.name: Express both weights through $\Phi_d$ of children ratios
nodes.statement: Let function $\Phi_d:\mathbb{R}^d\to \mathbb{R}$ be such that \begin{align} {\bf x} & \mapsto \frac{(\beta \gamma-1) \cdot F_d({\bf x})} {(\beta \cdot F_d({\bf x})+1)(F_d({\bf x})+\gamma)}\enspace, \end{align} while $F_d({\bf x})=F_d({\bf x}_1, \ldots, {\bf x}_d)$ is defined in \eqref{eq:BPRecursion}. Recall that $d$ is the number of children of vertex $v$. For each child $v_{i}$, consider the ratios of marginals $\blue{{R}}^{M, \sigma}_{v_{i}}$ and $\magenta{\overline{{R}}}^{L, \eta}_{v_{i}}$ defined as described in \Cref{sec:RecursionVsSpectralIneq}. Specifically, the ratio $\blue{{R}}^{M, \sigma}_{v_{i}}$ is defined with respect to the Gibbs distribution $\mu^{M,\sigma}_{\applegreen{T}}$, while the ratio $\magenta{\overline{{R}}}^{L, \eta}_{v_{i}}$ is defined with respect to the Gibbs distribution $\mu^{L,\eta}_{\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}}$. Using \eqref{def:OfInfluenceWeights}, it is not hard to verify that we have $\upalpha(f)=\Phi_d(\blue{{R}}^{M, \sigma}_{v_1}, \ldots, \blue{{R}}^{M, \sigma}_{v_d})$ and similarly $\upalpha_{P}(f)=\Phi_d(\magenta{\overline{{R}}}^{L,\eta}_{v_1},\ldots, \magenta{\overline{{R}}}^{L, \eta}_{v_d})$.
nodes.statement_short: Express both weights through $\Phi_d$ of children ratios

nodes.name: Mean value theorem reduces to closeness of ratios
nodes.statement: From the {\em mean value theorem}, there exists ${\bf z}\in \mathbb{R}^d$ such that \begin{align} \upalpha_{P}(f)&=\upalpha(f) + \sum^{d}_{i=1} \left . \frac{\partial }{\partial {\bf x}_{i}}\Phi_d({\bf x}) \right |_{{\bf x}={\bf z}} \cdot \left (\magenta{\overline{{R}}}^{L, \eta}_{v_{i}}-\blue{{R}}^{M, \sigma}_{v_{i}} \right )\enspace. \end{align} Recall that we take $f$ such that $\upalpha(f) \neq 0$. Our $b$-boundedness assumption, for fixed $b>0$, and having $ \upalpha(f) \neq 0$, imply that $\abs{\upalpha (f)}$ is a constant bounded away from zero. Hence, \eqref{eq:prop:StableSSM} is true if the sum on the r.h.s. in \eqref{eq:MeanValue4Alphas} is a sufficiently small constant.
nodes.statement_short: Mean value theorem reduces to closeness of ratios

nodes.name: The partial derivatives of $\Phi_d$ are bounded
nodes.statement: A standard calculation implies that for $i =1,\ldots, d$, we have \begin{align} \frac{\partial }{\partial {\bf x}_{i}}\Phi_d({\bf x}) &= \Phi_d({\bf x}) \cdot {\textstyle \frac{\beta\gamma-1}{(\beta {\bf x}_{i}+1)({\bf x}_{i}+\gamma)}} \cdot {\textstyle \left(1-\frac{1+\beta\gamma+2F_d({\bf x})}{\beta\gamma-1} \cdot \Phi_d({\bf x}) \right) }\enspace. \end{align} The above implies that $\frac{\partial }{\partial {\bf x}_{i}}\Phi_d({\bf x}) $ is bounded only if both $\Phi_d({\bf x})$ and $F_d({\bf x})$ are bounded for any ${\bf x}\in [0,\infty]^d$ and $d\in [{\Delta}]$. From the definition of the functions $\Phi_d({\bf x})$ and $F_d({\bf x})$, it follows that they are indeed bounded, implying that $\frac{\partial }{\partial {\bf x}_{i}}\Phi_d({\bf x}) $ is also bounded for $i =1,\ldots, d$.
nodes.statement_short: The partial derivatives of $\Phi_d$ are bounded

nodes.name: Reduce to ratio closeness (13.10)
nodes.statement: In light of all the above, \eqref{eq:prop:StableSSM} follows by showing that for any fixed number $\upkappa>0$, there is $\ell_0=\ell_0(\upkappa)$ such that for any edge $f$ at distance $\ell\geq \ell_0$ from set $\magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$, we have \begin{align} \abs{ \magenta{\overline{{R}}}^{L, \eta}_{v_{i}}-\blue{{R}}^{M, \sigma}_{v_{i}} } &\leq \upkappa & \textrm{for } 1\leq i\leq d\enspace. \end{align}

nodes.name: Lemmas 8.3 and 13.1 bound the ratio difference by a...
nodes.statement: Note that assuming that $f$ is at distance $\ell$ from $\magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$ implies that the ball of radius $\ell-1$ from each vertex $v_{i}$ is inside tree $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$. This follows from \Cref{lemma:Subtree4TSawU,lemma:BoundaryTVsBoundaryTPFromU}. Furthermore, statement \ref{stat:C-lemma:BoundaryTVsBoundaryTPFromU} in \Cref{lemma:BoundaryTVsBoundaryTPFromU} implies that there is a pair of configurations $\xi^{(i)}_1$ and $\xi^{(i)}_2$ at $N=L\cup \magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$, which only disagree at $\magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$, such that \begin{align} \abs{ \magenta{\overline{{R}}}^{L, \eta}_{v_{i}}-\blue{{R}}^{M, \sigma}_{v_{i}} } &\leq \abs{ \magenta{\overline{{R}}}^{N, \xi^{(i)}_1}_{v_{i}}-\magenta{\overline{{R}}}^{N, \xi^{(i)}_2}_{v_{i}} } & \textrm{for } 1\leq i\leq d \enspace, \end{align} where $\magenta{\overline{{R}}}^{N, \xi^{(i)}_1}_{z}$ and $\magenta{\overline{{R}}}^{N, \xi^{(i)}_2}_{z}$ are the ratios of marginals at vertex $z$ with respect to the Gibbs distributions $\mu^{N, \xi^{(i)}_1}_{\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}}$ and $\mu^{N, \xi^{(i)}_2}_{\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}}$, respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Lemmas 8.3 and 13.1 bound the ratio difference by a boundary-change difference

nodes.name: State Claim 13.6
nodes.statement: We bound the r.h.s. of \eqref{eq:RealRatiosVsTPRatios} by using the following result. \begin{claim} For $\delta= \frac{1-\varepsilon}{\uprho}$, suppose that there is a $(\darkmagenta{s},\delta,c)$-potential function ${\Psi}$ with respect to $(\beta,\gamma,\lambda)$, where $\varepsilon, \beta,\gamma, \lambda,\uprho$ are defined in \Cref{prop:StableSSM}. Then, there are constants $c_A, c_B>0$ and $t_0>0$, such that for any vertex $z$ in tree $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ which is at distance $\ell\geq t_0$ from $\magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$, the following is true: For $N=L\cup \magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$ and for {\em any} two configurations $\eta_1, \eta_2\in \{\pm 1\}^{N }$ that differ only at $\magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$, we have \begin{align} \abs{ \magenta{\overline{{R}}}^{N, \eta_1}_{z} - \magenta{\overline{{R}}}^{N, \eta_2}_{z}} \leq c_A \cdot \exp\left( -c_B \cdot \ell \right)\enspace, \end{align} where $\magenta{\overline{{R}}}^{N, \eta_1}_{z}$ and $\magenta{\overline{{R}}}^{N, \eta_2}_{z}$ are the ratios of marginals at vertex $z$ with respect to the Gibbs distributions $\mu^{N, \eta_1}_{\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}}$ and $\mu^{N, \eta_2}_{\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}}$, respectively. \end{claim}

nodes.name: Conclude from Claim 13.6
nodes.statement: We get \eqref{eq:Target4prop:StableSSM} from \eqref{eq:RealRatiosVsTPRatios} and \Cref{claim:Target4prop:StableSSM}. \Cref{prop:StableSSM} follows. \hfill $\square$

nodes.name: Neighbourhood $\uppi$ of $f$ lies in $\overline T$
nodes.statement: The proof is not too different from that of \Cref{claim:SupportOfWeiS} In this proof, we identify $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}=T_{\rm SAW}(\gext{G}{P},u)$ as a subtree of $\applegreen{T}=T_{\rm SAW}(G,u)$. W.l.o.g., let edge $f$ in $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ be such that $f=\{v,x\}$. Also, let $\uppi$ be the set of vertices that consists of $v,x$ and their children in $\applegreen{T}$. Arguing as in \Cref{claim:SupportOfWeiS}, the assumption of having $f$ at distance $>10$ from $\magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$ implies that all elements in $\uppi$ are vertices in $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$.

nodes.name: Zero weights come only from pinned neighbourhoods
nodes.statement: Our assumption for $b$-boundedness, for fixed $b>0$, implies that for edge $f$ in $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$, we either have $\upalpha(f)=0$, or $\abs{\upalpha(f)}$ is bounded away from zero. The same holds for $\upalpha_{P}(f)$. Furthermore, we have $\upalpha(f)=0$ (resp. $\upalpha_{P}(f)=0$) only if at least one of the vertices in $\uppi$ has a pinning under $\mu^{M,\sigma}_{\applegreen{T}}$ (resp. $\mu^{L,\eta}_{\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}}$). Note that for the case where the parameter of the Gibbs distribution $\beta=0$, it is possible that by pinning one of the children of $v$ or $x$ we get $\upalpha(f)=0$ (resp. $\upalpha_{P}(f)=0$).
nodes.statement_short: Zero weights come only from pinned neighbourhoods

nodes.name: Lemma 13.1 shows the pinnings on $\uppi$ coincide
nodes.statement: Recall from \Cref{lemma:BoundaryTVsBoundaryTPFromU}, statement \ref{stat:C-lemma:BoundaryTVsBoundaryTPFromU}, that the pinnings imposed by $\mu^{M,\sigma}_{\applegreen{T}}$ and $\mu^{L,\eta}_{\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}}$ on the vertices in $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ can only differ on the vertices in $L\setminus M\subseteq \byzantine{{\tt A}}_{P}$. But since $L\setminus M\subseteq \overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$, we have that $L\setminus M\subseteq \magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$, i.e., since statement \ref{stat:B-lemma:BoundaryTVsBoundaryTPFromU} in \Cref{lemma:BoundaryTVsBoundaryTPFromU} implies that $\byzantine{{\tt A}}_{P}\cap \overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}=\magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$. Taking $f$ at a sufficiently large distance from $\magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$, e.g., distance greater than $10$, we have that $\uppi\not\subset \magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$. Hence, if the two distributions $\mu^{M,\sigma}_{\applegreen{T}}$ and $\mu^{L,\eta}_{\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}}$ impose pinnings to vertices in set $\uppi$, these pinning should be identical.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 13.1 shows the pinnings on $\uppi$ coincide

nodes.name: Hence zero weights coincide
nodes.statement: This leads us to conclude that if $\upalpha(f)=0$, this is because $\mu^{M,\sigma}_{\applegreen{T}}$ fixes the configuration of a vertex in $\uppi$. But then, $\mu^{L,\eta}_{\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}}$ imposes identical pinning to $\uppi$. Hence, we also have $\upalpha_{P}(f)=0$. All the above conclude the proof of \Cref{claim:AlphaPZero}. \hfill $\square$

nodes.name: Bound walk counts $K(\ell)$ by entries of $H^{\ell-k}_{G,k}$
nodes.statement: In this proof, we identify $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}=T_{\rm SAW}(\gext{G}{P},u)$ as a subtree of $\applegreen{T}=T_{\rm SAW}(G,u)$. Firstly, we upper bound the number of paths in $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ from vertex $z$ to the set of vertices $\magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$ as a function of $\ell$, i.e., the distance of $z$ from the set. If $z$ is a copy of vertex $\widehat{z}$ in $\gext{G}{P}$, then the paths from $z$ to $\magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$ correspond to the self-avoiding walks from $\widehat{z}$ to the set of vertices $P\cup \cadmiumgreen{\UpS}_{P}$. Let $K(\ell)$ be the number of these walks. We assume that $\ell\geq t_0$ for a large constant $t_0$, e.g., $t_0>100k$. Note that $K(\ell)$ is upper bounded by the number of self-avoiding walks in $G$ from vertex $\widehat{z}$ to $P$. Furthermore, since each self-avoiding path of length $\ell>k$ is also a $k$-non-backtracking walk, we have \begin{align} K(\ell) &\leq\sum\nolimits_{W,Q}\cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k}^{\ell-k}(W,Q) \enspace. \end{align} Variable $W$ varies over the walks in $\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{k}$ which emanate from vertex $\widehat{z}$. Variable $Q$ varies over $\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{k}$ such that its last vertex is in $P$. The exponent $\ell-k$ has to do with how we measure distances between $k$-non-backtracking walks with $\cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k}$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound walk counts $K(\ell)$ by entries of $H^{\ell-k}_{G,k}$

nodes.name: Count summands
nodes.statement: A crude estimation implies that the number of summands in \eqref{eq:KEllVsNBMGPEntry} is $\leq (k+2)\cdot {\Delta}^{k}$. We have \begin{align} K(\ell) &\leq (k+2)\cdot {\Delta}^{k} \cdot \max\nolimits_{W,Q}\{ \cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k}^{\ell-k}(W,Q)\} \enspace. \end{align}

nodes.name: Claims 5.7, 5.8 give growth $((1+\zeta)\uprho)^r$
nodes.statement: Furthermore, \Cref{claim:SigmaLVsPathNumber,lemma:SingSequenConv} imply that for any $\zeta\in (0,1)$, there exists integer $\hat{r}_0=\hat{r}_0(N,{\Delta}, k, \zeta)>1$ such that for any $r \geq \hat{r}_0$ we have \begin{align} \cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k}^{r}(W,Q) \leq \left( (1+\zeta)\cdot \uprho \right)^{r}\enspace. \end{align} Recall that $\nnorm{ (\cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^N}{1/N}{2}=\uprho$. Combining \eqref{eq:KELLVMaxHGKWQ} and \eqref{eq:FromClaim5758}, for $\ell\geq \max\{\hat{r}_0,k\}$, we have \begin{align} K(\ell) & \leq (k+2)\cdot {\Delta}^{k}\cdot \left( (1+\zeta)\cdot \uprho \right)^{\ell-k} \enspace. \end{align}

nodes.name: Choose $\zeta$ and $t_0$ so $K(\ell)\le((1+\varepsilon/2)\uprho)^\ell$
nodes.statement: We choose $\zeta$ such that $\zeta=(1+\varepsilon/2)(1-\varepsilon/2)$, where $\varepsilon$ is from the parameter $\delta$ of the $(\darkmagenta{s},\delta,c)$-potential function ${\Psi}$, i.e., recall that we have $\delta= \frac{1-\varepsilon}{\uprho}$. We choose $t_0$ to be the maximum between the quantities $2\varepsilon^{-1}\log((k+2)\cdot {\Delta}^{k})$ and $\hat{r}_0$. With our choices of $\zeta$ and $t_0$, for any $\ell\geq t_0$, we have $K(\ell)\leq \left((1+\varepsilon/2)\cdot \uprho\right)^{\ell}$.

nodes.name: Standard potential-function contraction with $\Psi\circ\log$
nodes.statement: With the above in mind, standard arguments imply that for \eqref{eq:ClaimTarget4prop:StableSSM}, it suffices to show that there exists a differentiable, increasing potential function $\Upxi:[-\infty,+\infty]\to(-\infty,+\infty)$ such that \begin{align} \phi\left( F({\bf z})\right)\cdot \sum^d_{i=1} \frac{1}{\phi({\bf z}_{i})}\cdot \left. \frac{\partial}{\partial {\bf x}_{i}}F({\bf x})\right|_{{\bf x}={\bf z}} \cdot {\bf m}_{i} &\leq \left( \frac{1-\varepsilon}{\uprho}\right)^{1/\darkmagenta{s}} \cdot \norm{ {\bf m}}{\darkmagenta{s}}\enspace, \end{align} where $\phi=\Upxi'$. Using the standard chain rule for derivatives, (see also \cite{VigodaSpectralInd}) we conclude that \eqref{eq:SSMCondition4Stability} is true by using $\Upxi={\Psi}\circ\log$, where ${\Psi}$ is the $(\darkmagenta{s},\delta,c)$-potential function. \Cref{claim:Target4prop:StableSSM} follows. \hfill $\square$

nodes.name: Theorems 14.1, 3.7 and Claim 14.2 give $\rho(\mathcal{I})=O(1)$
nodes.statement: Combining \Cref{thrm:GoodPotentialHC}, \Cref{thrm:NonBacktrackingPotentialSpIn} and \Cref{claim:InterpretGoodPotentialHC}, with our assumption that ${\Delta}$ and $\uprho$ being $\Theta(1)$, we have \begin{align} \nonumber {\rho} {\textstyle \left( {\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G} \right)} &= O(1) \enspace, \end{align} for any $\Lambda\subset V$ and $\tau\in \{\pm 1\}^{\Lambda}$.

nodes.name: Marginal boundedness and Theorem 5.4
nodes.statement: Furthermore, our assumptions about $\lambda$ imply that $\mu$ is $b$-marginally bounded, for fixed $b>0$. Considering all the above, \Cref{thrm:HC4SPRadiusHash} follows as a corollary from \Cref{thrm:SPINLOGN}. \hfill $\square$

nodes.name: Theorems 14.1, 3.6 and Claim 14.2 give $\rho(\mathcal{I})=O(1)$
nodes.statement: The proof of \Cref{thrm:HC4SPRadiusAdj} is almost identical to that of \Cref{thrm:HC4SPRadiusHash}. Combining \Cref{thrm:GoodPotentialHC}, \Cref{thrm:AdjacencyPotentialSpIn} and \Cref{claim:InterpretGoodPotentialHC}, with our assumption about ${\Delta}$ and ${\varrho}$ being $\Theta(1)$, we have \begin{align} \nonumber {\rho} \left( {\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G} \right) &=O(1)\enspace, \end{align} for any $\Lambda\subset V$ and $\tau\in \{\pm 1\}^{\Lambda}$.

nodes.name: Marginal boundedness and Theorem 5.4
nodes.statement: Furthermore, our assumptions about $\lambda$ imply that $\mu$ is $b$-marginally bounded, for fixed $b>0$. Considering all the above, \Cref{thrm:HC4SPRadiusAdj} follows as a corollary from \Cref{thrm:SPINLOGN}. \hfill $\square$

nodes.name: State Proposition 14.3
nodes.statement: To prove \Cref{thrm:HC4CCK}, we use the following proposition. \begin{restatable}{proposition}{CcLccVsHSPradius} For integers $k,N>0$ and graph $G=(V,E)$, we have that $\norm{(\cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^N}{2} \leq \left( \goldenbrown{\upd}_{k}\right)^{N+k}$. \end{restatable} The proof of \Cref{prop:HSPRadCCLCC} appears in \Cref{sec:prop:HSPRadCCLCC}.

nodes.name: Choose $z$ with...
nodes.statement: Given the parameters $\varepsilon\in (0,1)$ and $\goldenbrown{\upd}_{k}$, let $z=z(\varepsilon, \goldenbrown{\upd}_{k})>0$ be such that \begin{align} {\lambda_c}((1+z)\goldenbrown{\upd}_k)= (1-\varepsilon/3){\lambda_c}(\goldenbrown{\upd}_k) \enspace. \end{align} Such $z$ exists and it is unique, since ${\lambda_c}(x)$ is monotonically decreasing in $x$.

nodes.name: Proposition 14.3 gives $\|H^N\|^{1/N}\le(1+z)\upd_k$
nodes.statement: \Cref{prop:HSPRadCCLCC} implies that there exists $M=M(z,\goldenbrown{\upd}_{k})$ such that for any $N\geq M$, we have \begin{align} \nnorm{ (\cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^N}{1/N}{2} \leq \left( \goldenbrown{\upd}_{k}\right)^{\frac{N+k}{N}}\leq (1+z)\goldenbrown{\upd}_{k}\enspace. \end{align}

nodes.name: Monotonicity gives...
nodes.statement: Let $\uprho=\nnorm{ (\cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^M}{1/M}{2}$, where $M$ is defined above. From \eqref{eq:Base4thrm:HC4CCK} and \eqref{eq:Base4thrm:HC4CCKBB} we have \begin{align} {\lambda_c}(\uprho) &\geq (1-\varepsilon/3){\lambda_c}(\goldenbrown{\upd}_k) \enspace. \end{align} For the above, we use once more that ${\lambda_c}(x)$ is monotonically decreasing in $x$.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem 1.2
nodes.statement: \Cref{thrm:HC4CCK} follows by noting that the above implies that for $\lambda<(1-\varepsilon){\lambda_c}(\goldenbrown{\upd}_k)$ we also have that $\lambda<(1-\varepsilon/3){\lambda_c}(\uprho)$. For such $\lambda$, \Cref{thrm:HC4SPRadiusHash} implies that there is a constant $C>0$, such that Glauber dynamics on the Hard-core model on $G$ has mixing time at most $C n\log n$. \hfill $\square$

nodes.name: Define $k$-wise self-avoiding walks
nodes.statement: Let integer $M>1$ which we will specify later. Let a length $k \cdot M$ walk $P=w_0, \ldots, w_{k \cdot M}$ in $G$. We say that $P$ is $k$-wise self-avoiding, if the sub-walk $P_{i}=w_{i\cdot k}, w_{i\cdot k+1}, \ldots, w_{i\cdot k+k}$ is self-avoiding, for all $i=0,\ldots, M-1$. Note that $P$ is not necessarily a self-avoiding walk since the same vertex $v$ can appear in both $P_{i}$ and $P_{j}$, for $i\neq j$.

nodes.name: Their number is at most $\upd_k^{kM}$
nodes.statement: For each $v\in V$, let $\uppi_{k}(v, k M)$ be the set of $k$-wise self-avoiding walks of length $k \cdot M$ that emanate from $v$. Let $\upchi_{k,M}=\sup\{ \uppi_{k}(v, k M)\ |\ v\in V\}$. It is an easy exercise to show that \begin{align} \upchi_{k, M} & \leq (\goldenbrown{\upd}_{k})^{k M}\enspace. \end{align}

nodes.name: Every $k$-non-backtracking walk is $k$-wise self-avoiding
nodes.statement: Furthermore, let $Q=x_{0}, \ldots, x_{k M}$ be a $k$-non-backtracking walk in $G$. $Q$ is also a $k$-wise self-avoiding walk. To see this, note that for all $j=0,\ldots, k\cdot(M-1)$, the sub-walk $x_{j},\ldots, x_{j+k}$ in $Q$ is self-avoiding. For $Q$ to be $k$-wise self-avoiding, we only need the sub-walks $x_{j},\ldots, x_{j+k}$ to be self-avoiding, for $j$ being a multiple of $k$. Hence, $Q$ is a $k$-wise self-avoiding walk.

nodes.name: Row sums of $H^{k(M-1)}$ bounded by $\upd_k^{kM}$
nodes.statement:
For $W, S\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{k}$, i.e., two self-avoiding walks of length $k$ in $G$, recall that $\cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k}^{k (M-1)}(W, S)$ is equal to the number of $k$-non-backtracking walks of length $k\cdot (M-1)$ that start from $W$ and end at $S$. Every $k$-non-backtracking walk of length $k\cdot (M-1)$ from $W$ to $S$ is also a $k$-wise self-avoiding walk of length $k\cdot M$ starting at $v$, the first vertex in $W$. Hence, we have  egin{align} \sum
olimits _{S\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{k}}\cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k}^{k(M-1)}(W, S) \leq \uppi_{k}(v, k M) \leq \upchi_{k, M} \enspace. \end{align} From all the above, we obtain  egin{align}
onumber 
orm{ (\cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^{k(M-1)}\cdot \UpR }{\infty}= 
orm{ (\cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^{k(M-1)}}{\infty} &\leq \upchi_{k,M}= (\goldenbrown{\upd}_{k})^{k M}\enspace, \end{align} where $\UpR$ is the involution defined in \eqref{def:OfInvolutation}.

nodes.name: Gelfand's formula on the symmetric $H^{k(M-1)}R$
Drop $R$ and set $M=N/k+1$
nodes.statement:
Since $\UpR$ is an involution, we have $
orm{ (\cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^{k(M-1)}\cdot \UpR}{2}=
orm{ (\cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^{k(M-1)}}{2}$. From the above, we conclude that $
orm{ (\cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^{k(M-1)}}{2} \leq \left(\goldenbrown{\upd}_{k}ight)^{k\cdot M}$. \Cref{prop:HSPRadCCLCC} follows by setting $M= rac{N}{k}+1$. \hfill $\square$

nodes.name: Lemma 15.1 gives $(1-\varepsilon)/\uprho$-contraction
Theorem 3.4 gives $\rho(\mathcal{I})=O(1)$
nodes.statement: The above, together with \Cref{thrm:NonBacktrackingInfinityMixing}, imply that for any $\Lambda\subset V$ and $\tau\in \{\pm 1\}^{\Lambda}$, the pairwise influence matrix ${\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G}$, induced by $\mu^{\Lambda,\tau}_G$, satisfies that \begin{align}\nonumber {\rho}({\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G})\leq \widehat{C} \cdot \varepsilon^{-1} \enspace, \end{align} for fixed number $\widehat{C}>0$. Clearly, we have ${\rho}({\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G})\in O(1)$.

nodes.name: Marginal boundedness and Theorem 5.4
nodes.statement: Furthermore, our assumptions about $\beta$ and $\lambda$ imply that $\mu_G$ is $b$-marginally bounded, for fixed $b>0$. Considering all the above, \Cref{thrm:Ising4SPRadiusHash} follows as a corollary from \Cref{thrm:SPINLOGN}. \hfill $\square$

nodes.name: Lemma 15.1 gives $(1-\varepsilon)/\varrho$-contraction
Theorem 3.2 gives $\rho(\mathcal{I})\le\varepsilon^{-1}$
nodes.statement: The above, combined with \Cref{thrm:AdjacencyInfinityMixing} imply that for $\Lambda\subset V$ and $\tau\in \{\pm 1\}^{\Lambda}$, the pairwise influence matrix ${\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G}$, induced by $\mu^{\Lambda,\tau}_G$, satisfies that \begin{align}\nonumber {\rho}({\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G})\leq \varepsilon^{-1}=O(1) \enspace. \end{align}

nodes.name: Marginal boundedness and Theorem 5.4
nodes.statement: Furthermore, our assumptions about $\beta$ and $\lambda$ imply that $\mu$ is $b$-marginally bounded, for fixed $b>0$. Considering all the above, \Cref{thrm:Ising4SPRadiusAdj} follows as a corollary from \Cref{thrm:SPINLOGN}. \hfill $\square$

nodes.name: Monotonicity of the uniqueness intervals in $z$ and $\delta$
nodes.statement: The proof of \Cref{thrm:Ising4CCK} is conceptually similar to \Cref{thrm:HC4CCK}. We are using \Cref{prop:HSPRadCCLCC} once more in this proof. It is straightforward to show that for any $z<\hat{z}$, we have ${\mathbb{U}_{\rm Ising}}(\hat{z},\delta)\subset {\mathbb{U}_{\rm Ising}}(z,\delta)$. Similarly, for any $\delta<\hat{\delta}$, we have ${\mathbb{U}_{\rm Ising}}(z,\hat{\delta})\subset {\mathbb{U}_{\rm Ising}}(z,\delta)$.
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity of the uniqueness intervals in $z$ and $\delta$

nodes.name: Choose $z$ matching the intervals
nodes.statement: Given the parameters $\varepsilon\in (0,1)$ and $\goldenbrown{\upd}_{k}$, let $z=z(\varepsilon, \goldenbrown{\upd}_{k})>0$ be such that \begin{align} {\mathbb{U}_{\rm Ising}}(\goldenbrown{\upd}_{k}, \varepsilon)= {\mathbb{U}_{\rm Ising}}((1+z)\goldenbrown{\upd}_{k}, \varepsilon/3)\enspace. \end{align}

nodes.name: Proposition 14.3 bounds $\uprho$ by $(1+z)\upd_k$
nodes.statement: Furthermore, \Cref{prop:HSPRadCCLCC} implies that there exists $M=M(z,\goldenbrown{\upd}_{k})$ such that for any $N\geq M$, we have \begin{align} \nnorm{(\cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^N}{1/N}{2} \leq \left( \goldenbrown{\upd}_{k}\right)^{\frac{N+k}{N}}\leq (1+z)\goldenbrown{\upd}_{k}\enspace. \end{align}

nodes.name: Interval inclusion...
nodes.statement: Let $\uprho=\nnorm{(\cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^M}{1/M}{2}$, where $M$ is defined above. The above relations imply that \begin{align} {\mathbb{U}_{\rm Ising}}(\goldenbrown{\upd}_{k}, \varepsilon)\subseteq {\mathbb{U}_{\rm Ising}}(\uprho, \varepsilon/3)\enspace. \end{align}

nodes.name: Apply the $H_{G,k}$ bound for the Ising model
nodes.statement: \Cref{thrm:Ising4CCK} follows by noting that the above relation implies that for $\beta\in {\mathbb{U}_{\rm Ising}}(\goldenbrown{\upd}_{k}, \varepsilon)$, we also have $\beta\in {\mathbb{U}_{\rm Ising}}(\uprho, \varepsilon/3)$. For such $\beta$ and for $\lambda>0$, \Cref{thrm:Ising4CCK} implies that there is a constant $C>0$, such that Glauber dynamics on the Ising model on $G$ has mixing time at most $C n\log n$. \hfill $\square$
nodes.statement_short: Apply the $H_{G,k}$ bound for the Ising model

nodes.name: Remove pinnings for the Hard-core model
nodes.statement: Recall that the ratio of Gibbs marginals ${R}^{\Lambda, \tau}_{u}$, defined in \Cref{sec:RecursionVsSpectralIneq}, is possible to be equal to zero, or $\infty$. Typically, this happens if vertex $u$ with respect to which we consider the ratio is pinned, i.e., $u \in \Lambda$, or has a neighbour in $\Lambda$. When we deal with the Hard-core model, there is a standard way to avoid these infinities and zeros in our calculations and make the derivation much simpler. Suppose we have the Hard-core model with fugacity $\lambda>0$ on a tree $T$, while at the set of vertices $\Lambda$ we have a pinning $\tau$. Then, it is elementary that this distribution is identical to the Hard-core model with the same fugacity on the tree (or forest) $T'$ which is obtained from $T$ by removing every vertex $w$ which either belongs to $\Lambda$, or has a neighbour in $ \Lambda$ which is pinned to 1. From now on, for the instances we consider, assume that we have applied the above steps and removed any pinnings.
nodes.statement_short: Remove pinnings for the Hard-core model

nodes.name: Write $F_d$, $F_{d,\rm sym}$, $H_d$, $h$, $J$ for the Hard-core model
nodes.statement: It is useful to write down the functions that arise from the tree recursions in \Cref{sec:RecursionVsSpectralIneq}, specifically for the Hard-core model with fugacity $\lambda$. Recall that, in this case, we have $\beta=0$ and $\gamma=1$. In the following definitions, we assume that there are no pinnings. For integer $d\geq 1$, we have $F_d:\mathbb{R}^d_{>0}\to (0, \lambda)$ such that for any ${\bf x}=({\bf x}_1, \ldots, {\bf x}_d)$, we have {\small \begin{align} {\bf x}\mapsto \lambda \prod\nolimits_{i\in [d]}\frac{1}{{\bf x}_{i}+1} \enspace. \end{align} } We also define $F_{d,{\rm sym}}:\mathbb{R}_{>0}\to (0, \lambda)$ the {\em symmetric} version of the above function, that is \begin{align} x&\mapsto F_d(x,x,\ldots, x) \enspace. \end{align} We also have $H_d:\mathbb{R}^d\to \mathbb{R}$ such that for any ${\bf x}=({\bf x}_1, \ldots, {\bf x}_d)$, we have {\small \begin{align} {\bf x} \mapsto \log \lambda+\sum\nolimits_{i\in [d]} \log\left( \frac{1}{\exp({\bf x}_{i})+1} \right) \enspace. \end{align} } For $\frac{\partial }{\partial {\bf x}_{i}}H_d({\bf x})=h({\bf x}_{i})$, we have $h:\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that {\small \begin{align} {\bf x} \mapsto -\frac{e^{{\bf x}_{i}}}{e^{{\bf x}_{i}}+1} \enspace. \end{align} } Finally, the set of log-ratios $J$, defined in \eqref{eq:DefOfRatiorange}, satisfies that \begin{align} J=(-\infty, \log(\lambda)) \enspace. \end{align} Set $S_{{\Psi}}$, i.e., the image of ${\Psi}$, satisfies $S_{{\Psi}}=(-\infty, \infty)$.
nodes.statement_short: Write $F_d$, $F_{d,\rm sym}$, $H_d$, $h$, $J$ for the Hard-core model

nodes.name: Reduce to Contraction and Boundedness
nodes.statement: \Cref{thrm:GoodPotentialHC} follows by showing that ${\Psi}$ satisfies the Contraction and the Boundedness conditions of \Cref{def:GoodPotential}, for the parameters indicated in the statement.

nodes.name: Define $\mathcal{R}_d$ and state Proposition 16.1
nodes.statement:
We start with the {\em Contraction}. For any integer $d>0$, we let ${\mathcal{R}}_{d}:\mathbb{R}^d	imes \mathbb{R}^d 	o \mathbb{R}$ be such that for ${ f m}=({ f m}_1, \ldots, { f m}_d)\in \mathbb{R}^{d}_{\geq 0}$, and ${ f \cadmiumgreen{y}}=({ f \cadmiumgreen{y}}_1, \ldots, { f \cadmiumgreen{y}}_d) \in \mathbb{R}^d$ we have {\small  egin{align} {\mathcal{R}}_{d}({ f m}, { f \cadmiumgreen{y}})={	extstyle \chi(H_{d}({ f \cadmiumgreen{y}})) }\sum^{d}_{j=1}  rac{ \abs{ h( { f \cadmiumgreen{y}}_j ) }}{ \chi( { f \cadmiumgreen{y}}_j )} 	imes { f m}_j \enspace, 
onumber \end{align} } where recall that $\chi={\Psi}'$. The following result implies that ${\Psi}$ satisfies the contraction condition.  egin{proposition}[Contraction] For $\delta$ and $s$ as defined in \Cref{thrm:GoodPotentialHC}, the following is true: for any integer $d>0$, for ${ f m}\in \mathbb{R}^{d}_{\geq 0}$, we have  egin{align} \sup
olimits_{{ f \cadmiumgreen{y}}\in (Q_{{\Psi}})^d }\{ {\mathcal{R}}_{d}({ f m}, { f y}) \} \leq \delta^{ rac{1}{s}} \cdot 
orm{ { f m}}{s} \enspace, \end{align} where $Q_{{\Psi}} \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ contains every $y \in \mathbb{R}$ such that there is $	ilde{y} \in S_{{\Psi}} $ for which we have ${y}={\Psi}^{-1}(	ilde{y})$. \end{proposition} The proof of \Cref{prop:PotContracts} appears in \Cref{sec:prop:PotContracts}.

nodes.name: Lemma 16.2 and its proof
nodes.statement: We now focus on establishing the {\em Boundedness} property of ${\Psi}$. \begin{lemma}[Boundedness] We have that $\textstyle \max_{\cadmiumgreen{y}_1, \cadmiumgreen{y}_2\in J }\left\{ \chi(\cadmiumgreen{y}_2) \cdot \frac{|h(\cadmiumgreen{y}_1)|}{\chi(\cadmiumgreen{y}_1)} \right\} \leq \frac{\lambda}{1+\lambda}$. \end{lemma} \begin{proof} Using the definitions of the functions $\chi$ and $h$ from \eqref{def:PotentialFunction} and \eqref{def:GradientRecHC}, respectively, we have {\small \begin{align} \max_{\cadmiumgreen{y}_1,\cadmiumgreen{y}_2\in J }\left\{ \chi(\cadmiumgreen{y}_2) \cdot \frac{|h(\cadmiumgreen{y}_1)|}{\chi(\cadmiumgreen{y}_1)} \right\} &= \max_{\cadmiumgreen{y}_1,\cadmiumgreen{y}_2\in J} \left\{\sqrt{h(\cadmiumgreen{y}_1)h(\cadmiumgreen{y}_2) } \right\} \ =\ \max_{\cadmiumgreen{y}_1,\cadmiumgreen{y}_2\in J} \left\{\sqrt{ \frac{e^{\cadmiumgreen{y}_1}}{1+e^{\cadmiumgreen{y}_1}}\frac{e^{\cadmiumgreen{y}_2}}{1+e^{\cadmiumgreen{y}_2}} } \right\} \ =\ { \frac{\lambda}{1+\lambda}} \enspace. \nonumber \end{align} } The last inequality follows from the observation that the function $g(x)=\frac{e^{x}}{1+e^{x}}$ is increasing in $x$, while, from \eqref{eq:RangeJ4HC}, we have that $e^{\cadmiumgreen{y}_1},e^{\cadmiumgreen{y}_2}\leq \lambda$. The claim follows. \end{proof}

nodes.name: Both conditions hold
nodes.statement: In light of \Cref{prop:PotContracts} and \Cref{lemma:PotBooundedness}, \Cref{thrm:GoodPotentialHC} follows. \hfill $\square$

nodes.name: Plan: bring $\mathcal{R}_d$ into the form of Sinclair et al.
nodes.statement: The proposition follows by using results from \cite{ConnectiveConst}. However, in order to apply these results, we need to bring ${\mathcal{R}}_{d}({\bf m}, {\bf y})$ into an appropriate form.
nodes.statement_short: Plan: bring $\mathcal{R}_d$ into the form of Sinclair et al.

nodes.name: Change variables $z=e^y$
nodes.statement:
For any $d>0$, we let ${\mathcal{J}}_{d}:\mathbb{R}^d_{\geq 0}	imes \mathbb{R}^d_{\geq 0}	o \mathbb{R}$ be such that for ${ f m}=({ f m}_1, \ldots, { f m}_d)\in \mathbb{R}^{d}_{\geq 0}$ and ${ f z}=({ f z}_1,\ldots, { f z}_d) \in \mathbb{R}^{d}_{\geq 0}$, we have {\small  egin{align} {\mathcal{J}}_{d}({ f m}, { f z}) &= \chi(\log F_{d}({ f z}) ) \sum
olimits_{j\in [d]}  rac{\abs{ h(\log { f z}_j )}}{ \chi( \log { f z}_j )} 	imes { f m}_j \enspace. 
onumber \end{align} } Using the definitions in \eqref{eq:HC-BPRecursion} and \eqref{eq:HC-DefOfH}, it is elementary to verify that for any $d>0$, for any ${ f m}\in \mathbb{R}^d_{\geq 0}$, ${ f z}\in \mathbb{R}^d_{>0}$ and ${ f y}\in \mathbb{R}^{d}$ such that ${ f z}_j=e^{{ f y}_j}$, we have that  egin{align}
onumber {\mathcal{J}}_{d}({ f m}, { f z})= {\mathcal{R}}_{d}({ f m}, { f y}) \enspace. \end{align} In light of the above, the proposition follows by showing that  egin{align} \sup
olimits_{{ f z}\in \mathbb{R}^d_{>0}} \{ {\mathcal{J}}_{d}({ f m}, { f z}) \} \leq \delta^{{1}/{\darkmagenta{s}}} \cdot 
orm{ { f m}}{\darkmagenta{s}} \enspace, \end{align} for $\darkmagenta{s}$ and $\delta$ indicated in \Cref{thrm:GoodPotentialHC}.

nodes.name: Define $\psi$
nodes.statement:
In order to prove \eqref{prop:Target4PotContractsA}, we let ${\psi}: \mathbb{R}_{>0}	o \mathbb{R}$ be such that {\small  egin{align} y& \mapsto  rac12\sqrt{ rac{1}{y(1+y)}} \enspace. \end{align} }  egin{claim} For any ${ f m}=({ f m}_1, \ldots, { f m}_d)\in \mathbb{R}^{d}_{ \geq 0}$ and ${ f z}=({ f z}_1, \ldots, { f z}_d)\in \mathbb{R}^{d}_{ > 0}$, we have {  egin{align} {\mathcal{J}}_{d}({ f m}, { f z})&= {\psi} (F_{d}({ f z})) 	imes \sum
olimits_{i\in [d]}  rac{{ f m}_i }{{\psi}({ f z}_i)} \left . \left|  rac{\partial }{\partial { f x}_i}F_{d}({ f x}) ight|_{{ f x} ={ f z}}ight| \enspace, \end{align} } where $F_{d}$ and ${\psi}$ are defined in \eqref{eq:HC-BPRecursion} and \eqref{def:PotentialFunction}, respectively. \end{claim}  egin{proof} The claim follows by using simple rearrangements. We have  egin{align} {\mathcal{J}}_{d}({ f m}, { f z}) &= \chi\left(\log F_{d}({ f z}) ight) \sum
olimits_{j\in [d]}  rac{ \abs{ h(\log { f z}_j )}}{ \chi\left( \log { f z}_j ight)} 	imes { f m}_j 
onumber\ &= \sqrt{ rac{F_{d}({ f z})}{1+F_{d}( f z)}} \sum^{d}_{j=1} \sqrt{ rac{{ f z}_j}{1+{ f z}_j}}	imes { f m}_j \ &= \sqrt{ rac{1}{F_{d}({ f z})(1+F_{d}( f z))}} \sum^{d}_{j=1} \sqrt{{ f z}_j(1+{ f z}_j) }	imes rac{ F_{d}( f z)}{1+{ f z}_j} 	imes { f m}_j \enspace. 
onumber \end{align} In \eqref{eq:AppOfFX}, we substitute $\chi$ and $h$ according to \eqref{def:XPotentialFunction} and \eqref{def:GradientRecHC}, respectively. Using the definition of ${\psi} $ from \eqref{def:PotentialFunction}, we get that  egin{align} {\mathcal{J}}_{d}({ f m}, { f z}) &= {\psi}(F_{d}({ f z})) \sum
olimits_{j\in [d]} rac{1}{ {\psi}({ f z}_j)} 	imes  rac{ F_{d}( f z)}{1+{ f z}_i} 	imes { f m}_j \enspace. 
onumber \end{align} The above implies \eqref{eq:SubCondVsPotentials}, i.e., since $\left|  rac{\partial }{\partial { f x}_i}F_{d}({ f x}) ight|= rac{F_{d}({ f x})}{1+{ f x}_i}$, for any $i\in [d]$. The claim follows. \end{proof}

nodes.name: Reduce to (16.11)
nodes.statement:
In light of \Cref{claim:OnePotVsOtherPot}, \eqref{prop:Target4PotContractsA} follows by showing that for any ${ f m}=({ f m}_1, \ldots, { f m}_d) \in \mathbb{R}^{d}_{ \geq 0}$ and ${ f z}=({ f z}_1, \ldots, { f z}_d)\in \mathbb{R}^{d}_{>0}$ we have  egin{align} {\psi} (F_{d}({ f z})) 	imes \sum
olimits_{i\in [d]}  rac{{ f m}_i }{{\psi}({ f z}_i)} \left . \left|  rac{\partial }{\partial { f x}_i}F_{d}({ f x}) ight|_{{ f x} ={ f z}}ight| & \leq \delta^{ rac{1}{s}} \cdot 
orm{ { f m}}{\darkmagenta{s}} \enspace. \end{align} 
oindent From our choice of the potential function, the above follows by using standard results form \cite{ConnectiveConst}.

nodes.name: Define $\Xi$ and recall Lemma 16.4
Recall Lemma 16.5
nodes.statement: In light of the above lemma, our proposition follows as a corollary from the following result. \begin{lemma}[\cite{ConnectiveConst}] For $\lambda>0$, consider ${\Delta_c}={\Delta_c}(\lambda)$ and $F_{{\Delta_c}, {\rm sym}}$ with fugacity $\lambda$. Let $\darkmagenta{s}\geq 1$ be such that {\small \begin{align}\nonumber \darkmagenta{s}^{-1}&= 1-{\textstyle \frac{{\Delta_c}-1}{2}}\cdot \log\left(1+{\textstyle \frac{1}{{\Delta_c}-1}} \right) \enspace. \end{align} } For any $x> 0$, $d> 0$, we have that ${\Xi}(\darkmagenta{s},d,x) \leq ({\Delta_c})^{-1}$. \end{lemma}

nodes.name: Combine Lemmas 16.4 and 16.5
nodes.statement: By combining \Cref{lemma:InsteadOfHolder,lemma:XiBoundAtFixPoint} we get \eqref{prop:Target4PotContractsB} for $\darkmagenta{s}$ as indicated in \Cref{lemma:XiBoundAtFixPoint} and $\delta=({\Delta_c})^{-1}$. This concludes the proof of \Cref{prop:PotContracts}. \hfill $\square$

nodes.name: Only the Hard-core case is shown
nodes.statement: The proofs of \Cref{thrm:HarndessTransHCNBM,thrm:HarndessTransIsingNBM} are almost identical. We only show how to prove \Cref{thrm:HarndessTransHCNBM} and we omit the proof of \Cref{thrm:HarndessTransIsingNBM}.
nodes.statement_short: Only the Hard-core case is shown

nodes.name: Define the Hard-core partition function
nodes.statement: For a graph $G=(V,E)$ and $\lambda>0$, consider the Hard-core model with fugacity $\lambda$. We define $\mathcal{Z}(G,\lambda)$, the {\em partition function} of this distribution by \begin{align} \mathcal{Z}(G,\lambda)&=\sum\nolimits_{\sigma}\lambda^{|\sigma|}\enspace, \end{align} where $\sigma$ varies over all the independent sets of $G$.

nodes.name: Recall the hardness Theorem 17.1
nodes.statement: For the proof of \Cref{thrm:HarndessTransHCNBM} we use the following result. \begin{theorem}[\cite{GSV16Hardness,SS14}] Unless ${\rm NP} = {\rm RP}$, for the Hard-core model, for all ${\Delta}\geq 3$ for all $\lambda>{\lambda_c}({\Delta}-1)$ there does not exist an FPRAS for the partition function with fugacity $\lambda$ for graphs of maximum degree at most ${\Delta}$. \end{theorem}

nodes.name: Positive part: Theorem 1.2 gives an $O^*(n^2)$ FPRAS
nodes.statement: \Cref{thrm:HC4SPRadiusHash} yields (via \cite{JVV86,SVV09}) an FPRAS for estimating the partition function $\mathcal{Z}(G,\lambda)$ with running time $O^*(n^2)$, for any $\lambda\leq (1-\varepsilon){\lambda_c}(\uprho)$. Recall that $\uprho=\nnorm{ (\cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^N}{1/N}{2}$. Also, recall that $O^*()$ hides multiplicative $\log n$-factors.
nodes.statement_short: Positive part: Theorem 1.2 gives an $O^*(n^2)$ FPRAS

nodes.name: Negative part: apply Theorem 17.1 with $\Delta=\lceil\uprho\rceil+1$
nodes.statement: The negative part, i.e., the non-existence of FPRAS for $\lambda\geq (1+\varepsilon){\lambda_c}(\lceil \uprho\rceil)$, follows from \Cref{thrm:HarndessCounting}. For graph $G$, such that $\nnorm{ (\cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^N}{1/N}{2}=\uprho$, it is standard that ${\Delta}\geq \lceil \uprho \rceil +1$. Then, it suffices to apply \Cref{thrm:HarndessCounting} for graphs $G$ with $\nnorm{ (\cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^N}{1/N}{2}=\uprho$ and maximum degree at most ${\Delta}=\lceil \uprho \rceil +1$. The above concludes the proof of \Cref{thrm:HarndessTransHCNBM}.

nodes.name: Define the semi-extended influence matrix $\mathcal{F}$
nodes.statement: For $G=(V,E)$, the Gibbs distribution $\mu^{\Lambda,\tau}_G$ and integer $k\geq 1$, we introduce the $\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}\times (V\setminus \Lambda)$ matrix ${\mathcal{F}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G,k}$ such that, for any $P \in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda, k}$ and $u\in V\setminus \Lambda$, the entry ${\mathcal{F}}^{\Lambda, \tau}_G(P, u) $ is defined as follows: Letting $w$ be the starting vertex of walk $P$, we have \begin{align} {\mathcal{F}}^{\Lambda, \tau}_{G,k}(P, u) &=0 \enspace, \end{align} if vertices $u$ and $w$ are at distance $<2k$. Consider $u$ and $w$ which are at distance $\geq 2k$. Let $\upzeta^{P}$ be the $P$-extension of $\mu^{\Lambda,\tau}_G$. We have \begin{align} {\mathcal{F}}^{\Lambda, \tau}_{G,k}(P, u) &= \upzeta^{P}_{u}(+1\ |\ (w,+1)) - \upzeta^{P}_{u}(+1 \ |\ (w,-1)) \enspace, \end{align} where $\upzeta^{P}_{u}$ is the marginal of $\upzeta^{P}$ at vertex $u$. Letting ${\mathcal{I}}^{P}$ be the influence matrix induced by $\upzeta^{P}$, \eqref{def:EdgeInflMatrixB} implies \begin{align} {\mathcal{F}}^{\Lambda, \tau}_{G,k}(P, u) &={\mathcal{I}}^{P}(w,u)\enspace. \end{align}

nodes.name: State Lemma 18.1
nodes.statement: In light of all the above, \Cref{thrm:InflVsExtInfl} follows as a corollary from the following two results. \begin{lemma} There is an $\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}\times (V\setminus \Lambda)$ matrix ${\mathcal{N}}_A$ such that \begin{align} {\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_G = \UpD_{k} \cdot\left({\mathcal{N}}_A \circ {\mathcal{F}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G,k} \right)+ {\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G, <2k} \enspace. \end{align} Furthermore, there is a fixed number $C_A>0$, which is independent of $\Lambda$ and $\tau$, such that, for any $P\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ and any $v\in V\setminus \Lambda$, we have $|{\mathcal{N}}_A(P,v)|\leq C_A$. \end{lemma} In \eqref{eq:lemma:FromCalI2CalF}, the matrices $ {\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G, <2{k}}$ and $\UpD_{k}$ are defined in \eqref{eq:DefOfCISmallerK} and \eqref{def:Vertex2EdgeMatrixEntryBB}, respectively. Also, ${\mathcal{N}}_A \circ {\mathcal{F}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G,k}$ is the Hadamard product of the two matrices. The proof of \Cref{lemma:FromCalI2CalF} appears in \Cref{sec:lemma:FromCalI2CalF}.

nodes.name: State Lemma 18.2
nodes.statement: \begin{lemma} There exists an $\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda, k}\times \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda, k}$ matrix ${\mathcal{N}}_B$ such that \begin{align} {\mathcal{F}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G,k} =\left( \applegreen{{\mathcal{L}}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G,k} \circ {\mathcal{N}}_B \right)\cdot \UpC_{k} \enspace. \end{align} Furthermore, there is a fixed number $C_B>0$, which is independent of $\Lambda$ and $\tau$, such that for any $Q,P\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$, we have $\abs{{\mathcal{N}}_B(P,Q)} \leq C_B$. \end{lemma} In \eqref{eq:lemma:FromCalF2CalH}, matrix $\UpC_k$ is defined in \eqref{def:Edge2VertexMatrixEntryBB}. The proof of \Cref{lemma:FromCalF2CalH} appears in \Cref{sec:lemma:FromCalF2CalH}.

nodes.name: Compose via $\mathcal{N}=\mathcal{N}_C\circ\mathcal{N}_B$
nodes.statement: \Cref{thrm:InflVsExtInfl} follows as a corollary from \Cref{lemma:FromCalI2CalF,lemma:FromCalF2CalH}. Specifically, ${\mathcal{N}}$ is given by the Hadamard product ${\mathcal{N}}={\mathcal{N}}_C \circ{\mathcal{N}}_B$, where ${\mathcal{N}}_B$ is from \Cref{lemma:FromCalF2CalH} and ${\mathcal{N}}_C$ is the $\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}\times \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ matrix such that for any $P,Q\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ we have ${\mathcal{N}}_C(P,Q)={\mathcal{N}}_A(P,u)$, where $u$ is the starting vertex of $Q$. Matrix ${\mathcal{N}}_A$ is from \Cref{lemma:FromCalI2CalF}. We conclude that \Cref{thrm:InflVsExtInfl} is true for $\widehat{C}=C_A\cdot C_B$. \hfill $\square$

nodes.name: Abbreviations
nodes.statement: In this proof, we use the properties of extensions from \Cref{lemma:TsawPVsTsaw,lemma:GibbsWeightsTpVsP}. Also, we abbreviate $\UpD_{k}$, ${\mathcal{F}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G,k}$, ${\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G, <2k}$ and ${\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G}$ to $ \UpD$, ${\mathcal{F}}$, ${\mathcal{I}}_{<2k}$ and ${\mathcal{I}}$, respectively. Firstly, we note that the matrices at the two sides of the equation in \eqref{eq:lemma:FromCalI2CalF} are of the same dimension, i.e., they are $(V\setminus \Lambda)\times (V\setminus \Lambda)$.
nodes.statement_short: Abbreviations; both sides have the same dimension

nodes.name: Entrywise equality of both sides
nodes.statement:
We show that their corresponding entries are equal to each other. For any $v\in V\setminus \Lambda$, we have  egin{align} {\mathcal{I}}_{<2{k}}(v,v)&=1& 	extrm{and}&& \left(\UpD\cdot \left({\mathcal{N}}_A \circ{\mathcal{F}} ight)ight)(v,v)&=0 \enspace. \end{align} The equality on the right is true because $\left(\UpD\cdot \left({\mathcal{N}}_A \circ{\mathcal{F}} ight)ight)(v,v)=\sum_{P}\UpD(v,P)\cdot{\mathcal{N}}_A(P,v)\cdot {\mathcal{F}}(P,v)$ and the variable $P\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ runs over walks that emanate from $v$. For such walks ${\mathcal{F}}(P,v)=0$. Hence, for any matrix ${\mathcal{N}}_A$ the above is true. From the definition of ${\mathcal{I}}$ and \eqref{eq:FirstEqInlemma:FromCalI2CalF} we conclude that ${\mathcal{I}}$ and $ {\mathcal{I}}_{<2k}+\UpD\cdot\left({\mathcal{N}}_A \circ {\mathcal{F}} ight)$ have ones at their diagonal. Now, we focus on the off-diagonal elements. Let  egin{align} {\mathcal{I}}_{\geq 2k} &={\mathcal{I}}-{\mathcal{I}}_{<2k}\enspace. \end{align} It suffices to show that there exists an $\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}	imes V\setminus \Lambda$ matrix ${\mathcal{N}}_A$, with its entries bounded as specified in the statement of \Cref{lemma:FromCalI2CalF}, such that for any $u,w\in V\setminus \Lambda$, which are different from each other, we have  egin{align} {\mathcal{I}}_{\geq 2k}(w,u) &= \sum
olimits_{P} {\mathcal{N}}_A(P,u) \cdot {\mathcal{F}}(P,u) \enspace, \end{align} where $P$ varies in $\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda, k}$, such that its first vertex is $w$. For vertices $w,u\in V\setminus \Lambda$ at distance $< 2k$, The definition of ${\mathcal{F}}$ implies that for $P$ emanating from $w$, we have $ {\mathcal{F}}(P,u)=0$. Also, we have ${\mathcal{I}}_{\geq 2k}(w,u)=0$. We conclude that for pairs of vertices $w,u\in V\setminus \Lambda$ at distance $< 2k$, \eqref{eq:Target4lemma:FromCalI2CalF} is true for any choice of matrix ${\mathcal{N}}_A$. We consider $w$ and $u$ at distance $\geq 2k$ from each other. Let $ yzantine{T}=T_{{m SAW}}(G, w)$. Also, let $\{\upalpha(e)\}$ be the collection of weights over the edges of $ yzantine{T}$ we obtain by applying the $T_{m SAW}$-construction on the Gibbs distribution $\mu^{\Lambda,	au}_G$. Then, \Cref{prop:Inf2TreeRedaux} implies  egin{align} {\mathcal{I}}_{\geq 2k}(w,u) &=\sum
olimits_{\ell\geq 2k} \sum
olimits_{W=(e_1, \ldots, e_{\ell}) \in  yzantine{T}} \prod
olimits_{1 \leq i\leq \ell}\upalpha(e_{i}) \enspace, \end{align} where $W$ varies over the length-$\ell$ paths in $ yzantine{T}$ from the root of the tree to the copies of vertex $u$. For each $P\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$, which emanates from vertex $w$, consider $\deeppink{T_{P}}=T_{m SAW}(\gext{G}{P},w)$. Using \Cref{lemma:TsawPVsTsaw}, we identify each $\deeppink{T_{P}}$ as a subtree of $ yzantine{T}$, while note that both trees have the same root. Recall also the weights $\{\upalpha(e)\}$ on the edges of $ yzantine{T}$ that are induced by the $T_{m SAW}$-construction on $\mu^{\Lambda,	au}_G$. Since $\deeppink{T_{P}}$ is a subtree of $ yzantine{T}$, we endow $\deeppink{T_{P}}$ with the edge-weights $\{\upalpha(e)\}_{e\in \deeppink{T_{P}}}$. Each path $W$ in $ yzantine{T}$ that emanates from the root and is of length $\geq 2k$ belongs to exactly one of the subtrees $\deeppink{T_{P}}$ of $ yzantine{T}$ we define above. Using this observation, we write \eqref{eq:IfVsWeightscFVsVi} as follows:  egin{align} {\mathcal{I}}_{\geq 2k}(w,u)&=\sum
olimits_{P} \sum
olimits_{\ell \geq 2k} \sum
olimits_{W=(e_1,\ldots, e_{\ell}) \in \deeppink{T_{P}}} \prod
olimits_{1\leq i\leq \ell }\upalpha(e_i) \enspace, \end{align} where variable $P$ varies over the walks in $\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ that emanate from vertex $w$ and variable $W$ varies over the length-$\ell$ paths in $\deeppink{T_{P}}=T_{m SAW}(\gext{G}{P},w)$ from the root of the tree to the copies of vertex $u$. For each $P\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda, k}$ whose first vertex is $w$, and $\deeppink{T_{P}}=T_{m SAW}(\gext{G}{P},w)$, we let $\{\upalpha_{P}(e)\}_{e\in \deeppink{T_{P}}}$ be the collection of weights over the edges of $\deeppink{T_{P}}$ specified with respect to the $P$-extension of $\mu^{\Lambda,	au}_G$. The definition of matrix ${\mathcal{F}}$ in \eqref{def:EdgeInflMatrix} and \Cref{prop:Inf2TreeRedaux} imply  egin{align} {\mathcal{F}}(P, u)&=\sum
olimits_{\ell \geq 2k}\sum
olimits_{W=(e_1,\ldots, e_{\ell}) \in \deeppink{T_{P}}} \prod
olimits_{1\leq i\leq \ell} \upalpha_{P}(e_{i}) \enspace, \end{align} where $W$ varies over the length-$\ell$ paths from the root to the copies of $u$ in $\deeppink{T_{P}}$. Letting $P=x_0,\ldots,x_k$, there is a path $R_{P}=u_0,\ldots, u_{k}$ in tree $\magenta{T}$, which emanates from the root such that $u_{i}$ is a copy of $x_{i}$, for all $0\leq i \leq k $. We have that $R_{P}$ is in $ \deeppink{T_{P}}$, too. Furthermore, all paths $W\in \deeppink{T_{P}}$ of length $\ell\geq 2k$ that emanate from the root of $\deeppink{T_{P}}$ overlap with $R_{P}$ in their first $k$ edges.
