The above observation implies that fixing $\ell\geq 2k$ and path $W=(e_1,\ldots, e_{\ell})$, the corresponding summand in \eqref{eq:FVsITs} trivially satisfies  egin{align} \prod
olimits_{1\leq i\leq \ell} \upalpha_{P}(e_{i}) &= \UpK 	imes \prod
olimits_{k< i\leq \ell } \upalpha_{P}(e_{i}) \enspace, \end{align} where $\UpK=\prod
olimits_{e \in R_{P}} \upalpha_{P}(e)$. In a previous step, we endowed each $\deeppink{T_{P}}$ with the edge weights $\{\upalpha(e)\}_{e\in \deeppink{T_{P}}}$ since it is a subtree of $ yzantine{T}$. Overall now, for each $\deeppink{T_{P}}$ we have two sets of edges weights i.e., we have $\{\upalpha(e)\}_{e\in \deeppink{T_{P}}}$ and $\{\upalpha_{P}(e)\}_{e\in \deeppink{T_{P}}}$. \Cref{lemma:GibbsWeightsTpVsP} implies that for any edge $e\in \deeppink{T_{P}}$, which is at distance $\geq k$ from the root of $\deeppink{T_{P}}$, we have  egin{align} \upalpha_{P}(e)&=\upalpha(e) \enspace. \end{align} Combining \eqref{eq:IfVsWeightscFVsViCC} and \eqref{eq:ProdWeigtPTPBreak} we get the following: fixing $\ell\geq 2k$ and path $W=(e_1,\ldots, e_{\ell})$, the corresponding summand in \eqref{eq:FVsITs} satisfies  egin{align} \prod
olimits_{1\leq i\leq \ell} \upalpha_{P}(e_{i}) &= \UpK 	imes \prod
olimits_{k< i\leq \ell } \upalpha(e_{i}) \enspace. \end{align} We define the $\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}	imes V\setminus \Lambda$ matrix ${\mathcal{N}}_A$ such that for each $P\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ and $u\in V\setminus \Lambda$, we have  egin{align} {\mathcal{N}}_A(P,u) = \left \{  egin{array}{lcl} 1 &\quad &	extrm{if distance from $u$ to the starting vertex of $P$ is $<2k$}\ \prod_{e\in R_{P}} rac{\upalpha(e)}{\upalpha_{P}(e)+\mathds{1}\{\upalpha_{P}(e)=0\}} &&	extrm{otherwise}\enspace, \end{array} ight . 
onumber \end{align} where $R_{P}$ is the path in $\deeppink{T_{P}}$ defined earlier. The above definition of ${\mathcal{N}}_A$ implies  egin{align} {\mathcal{N}}_A(P,u)\cdot {\mathcal{F}}(P, u)&= \sum
olimits_{\ell\geq 2k} \sum
olimits_{W=(e_1,\ldots, e_{\ell})\in \deeppink{T_{P}}} \prod
olimits_{1\leq i\leq \ell }\upalpha(e_{i}) \enspace, \end{align} where $W$ varies over the paths in $\deeppink{T_{P}}$ from the root to the copies of vertex $u$ at distance $\ell$ from the root. Verifying the above equality is a matter of simple calculations when $\upalpha_{P}(e)
eq 0$ for all $e\in R_{P}$. That is, it follows from \eqref{eq:FVsITs}, \eqref{eq:ProdWeigtPTPBreakNew} and the definition of ${\mathcal{N}}_A$. When there is at least one $e\in R_{P}$ such that $\upalpha_{P}(e)=0$, then it is not hard to see that we also have $\upalpha(e)=0$; hence both sides in \eqref{eq:IfVsWeightscFVsViDD} are equal to zero. All the above imply that \eqref{eq:IfVsWeightscFVsViDD} is true. Then, plugging \eqref{eq:IfVsWeightscFVsViDD} into \eqref{eq:IfVsWeightscFVsViBB}, we obtain \eqref{eq:Target4lemma:FromCalI2CalF}. Hence, we conclude that \eqref{eq:lemma:FromCalI2CalF} is true.

nodes.name: Diagonal entries agree
nodes.statement: For any $v\in V\setminus \Lambda$, we have \begin{align} {\mathcal{I}}_{<2{k}}(v,v)&=1& \textrm{and}&& \left(\UpD\cdot \left({\mathcal{N}}_A \circ{\mathcal{F}} \right)\right)(v,v)&=0 \enspace. \end{align} The equality on the right is true because $\left(\UpD\cdot \left({\mathcal{N}}_A \circ{\mathcal{F}} \right)\right)(v,v)=\sum_{P}\UpD(v,P)\cdot{\mathcal{N}}_A(P,v)\cdot {\mathcal{F}}(P,v)$ and the variable $P\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ runs over walks that emanate from $v$. For such walks ${\mathcal{F}}(P,v)=0$. Hence, for any matrix ${\mathcal{N}}_A$ the above is true. From the definition of ${\mathcal{I}}$ and \eqref{eq:FirstEqInlemma:FromCalI2CalF} we conclude that ${\mathcal{I}}$ and $ {\mathcal{I}}_{<2k}+\UpD\cdot\left({\mathcal{N}}_A \circ {\mathcal{F}} \right)$ have ones at their diagonal.

nodes.name: Reduce off-diagonal entries to (18.8)
nodes.statement: Now, we focus on the off-diagonal elements. Let \begin{align} {\mathcal{I}}_{\geq 2k} &={\mathcal{I}}-{\mathcal{I}}_{<2k}\enspace. \end{align} It suffices to show that there exists an $\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}\times V\setminus \Lambda$ matrix ${\mathcal{N}}_A$, with its entries bounded as specified in the statement of \Cref{lemma:FromCalI2CalF}, such that for any $u,w\in V\setminus \Lambda$, which are different from each other, we have \begin{align} {\mathcal{I}}_{\geq 2k}(w,u) &= \sum\nolimits_{P} {\mathcal{N}}_A(P,u) \cdot {\mathcal{F}}(P,u) \enspace, \end{align} where $P$ varies in $\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda, k}$, such that its first vertex is $w$.

nodes.name: Close pairs: both sides vanish
nodes.statement: For vertices $w,u\in V\setminus \Lambda$ at distance $< 2k$, The definition of ${\mathcal{F}}$ implies that for $P$ emanating from $w$, we have $ {\mathcal{F}}(P,u)=0$. Also, we have ${\mathcal{I}}_{\geq 2k}(w,u)=0$. We conclude that for pairs of vertices $w,u\in V\setminus \Lambda$ at distance $< 2k$, \eqref{eq:Target4lemma:FromCalI2CalF} is true for any choice of matrix ${\mathcal{N}}_A$.

nodes.name: Far pairs: expand $\mathcal{I}_{\ge2k}$ over $T_{\rm SAW}$ paths
nodes.statement:
We consider $w$ and $u$ at distance $\geq 2k$ from each other. Let $ yzantine{T}=T_{{m SAW}}(G, w)$. Also, let $\{\upalpha(e)\}$ be the collection of weights over the edges of $ yzantine{T}$ we obtain by applying the $T_{m SAW}$-construction on the Gibbs distribution $\mu^{\Lambda,	au}_G$. Then, \Cref{prop:Inf2TreeRedaux} implies  egin{align} {\mathcal{I}}_{\geq 2k}(w,u) &=\sum
olimits_{\ell\geq 2k} \sum
olimits_{W=(e_1, \ldots, e_{\ell}) \in  yzantine{T}} \prod
olimits_{1 \leq i\leq \ell}\upalpha(e_{i}) \enspace, \end{align} where $W$ varies over the length-$\ell$ paths in $ yzantine{T}$ from the root of the tree to the copies of vertex $u$.
nodes.statement_short: Far pairs: expand $\mathcal{I}_{\ge2k}$ over $T_{\rm SAW}$ paths

nodes.name: Partition the paths among the subtrees $T_P$
nodes.statement:
For each $P\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$, which emanates from vertex $w$, consider $\deeppink{T_{P}}=T_{m SAW}(\gext{G}{P},w)$. Using \Cref{lemma:TsawPVsTsaw}, we identify each $\deeppink{T_{P}}$ as a subtree of $ yzantine{T}$, while note that both trees have the same root. Recall also the weights $\{\upalpha(e)\}$ on the edges of $ yzantine{T}$ that are induced by the $T_{m SAW}$-construction on $\mu^{\Lambda,	au}_G$. Since $\deeppink{T_{P}}$ is a subtree of $ yzantine{T}$, we endow $\deeppink{T_{P}}$ with the edge-weights $\{\upalpha(e)\}_{e\in \deeppink{T_{P}}}$. Each path $W$ in $ yzantine{T}$ that emanates from the root and is of length $\geq 2k$ belongs to exactly one of the subtrees $\deeppink{T_{P}}$ of $ yzantine{T}$ we define above. Using this observation, we write \eqref{eq:IfVsWeightscFVsVi} as follows:  egin{align} {\mathcal{I}}_{\geq 2k}(w,u)&=\sum
olimits_{P} \sum
olimits_{\ell \geq 2k} \sum
olimits_{W=(e_1,\ldots, e_{\ell}) \in \deeppink{T_{P}}} \prod
olimits_{1\leq i\leq \ell }\upalpha(e_i) \enspace, \end{align} where variable $P$ varies over the walks in $\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ that emanate from vertex $w$ and variable $W$ varies over the length-$\ell$ paths in $\deeppink{T_{P}}=T_{m SAW}(\gext{G}{P},w)$ from the root of the tree to the copies of vertex $u$.
nodes.statement_short: Partition the paths among the subtrees $T_P$

nodes.name: Expand $\mathcal{F}(P,u)$ and factor out the first $k$ weights
nodes.statement:
For each $P\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda, k}$ whose first vertex is $w$, and $\deeppink{T_{P}}=T_{m SAW}(\gext{G}{P},w)$, we let $\{\upalpha_{P}(e)\}_{e\in \deeppink{T_{P}}}$ be the collection of weights over the edges of $\deeppink{T_{P}}$ specified with respect to the $P$-extension of $\mu^{\Lambda,	au}_G$. The definition of matrix ${\mathcal{F}}$ in \eqref{def:EdgeInflMatrix} and \Cref{prop:Inf2TreeRedaux} imply  egin{align} {\mathcal{F}}(P, u)&=\sum
olimits_{\ell \geq 2k}\sum
olimits_{W=(e_1,\ldots, e_{\ell}) \in \deeppink{T_{P}}} \prod
olimits_{1\leq i\leq \ell} \upalpha_{P}(e_{i}) \enspace, \end{align} where $W$ varies over the length-$\ell$ paths from the root to the copies of $u$ in $\deeppink{T_{P}}$. Letting $P=x_0,\ldots,x_k$, there is a path $R_{P}=u_0,\ldots, u_{k}$ in tree $\magenta{T}$, which emanates from the root such that $u_{i}$ is a copy of $x_{i}$, for all $0\leq i \leq k $. We have that $R_{P}$ is in $ \deeppink{T_{P}}$, too. Furthermore, all paths $W\in \deeppink{T_{P}}$ of length $\ell\geq 2k$ that emanate from the root of $\deeppink{T_{P}}$ overlap with $R_{P}$ in their first $k$ edges. The above observation implies that fixing $\ell\geq 2k$ and path $W=(e_1,\ldots, e_{\ell})$, the corresponding summand in \eqref{eq:FVsITs} trivially satisfies  egin{align} \prod
olimits_{1\leq i\leq \ell} \upalpha_{P}(e_{i}) &= \UpK 	imes \prod
olimits_{k< i\leq \ell } \upalpha_{P}(e_{i}) \enspace, \end{align} where $\UpK=\prod
olimits_{e \in R_{P}} \upalpha_{P}(e)$.
nodes.statement_short: Expand $\mathcal{F}(P,u)$ and factor out the first $k$ weights

nodes.name: Lemma 8.2: weights agree beyond depth $k$
nodes.statement: In a previous step, we endowed each $\deeppink{T_{P}}$ with the edge weights $\{\upalpha(e)\}_{e\in \deeppink{T_{P}}}$ since it is a subtree of $\byzantine{T}$. Overall now, for each $\deeppink{T_{P}}$ we have two sets of edges weights i.e., we have $\{\upalpha(e)\}_{e\in \deeppink{T_{P}}}$ and $\{\upalpha_{P}(e)\}_{e\in \deeppink{T_{P}}}$. \Cref{lemma:GibbsWeightsTpVsP} implies that for any edge $e\in \deeppink{T_{P}}$, which is at distance $\geq k$ from the root of $\deeppink{T_{P}}$, we have \begin{align} \upalpha_{P}(e)&=\upalpha(e) \enspace. \end{align} Combining \eqref{eq:IfVsWeightscFVsViCC} and \eqref{eq:ProdWeigtPTPBreak} we get the following: fixing $\ell\geq 2k$ and path $W=(e_1,\ldots, e_{\ell})$, the corresponding summand in \eqref{eq:FVsITs} satisfies \begin{align} \prod\nolimits_{1\leq i\leq \ell} \upalpha_{P}(e_{i}) &= \UpK \times \prod\nolimits_{k< i\leq \ell } \upalpha(e_{i}) \enspace. \end{align}

nodes.name: Define $\mathcal{N}_A$ and verify (18.15)
nodes.statement:
We define the $\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}	imes V\setminus \Lambda$ matrix ${\mathcal{N}}_A$ such that for each $P\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ and $u\in V\setminus \Lambda$, we have  egin{align} {\mathcal{N}}_A(P,u) = \left \{  egin{array}{lcl} 1 &\quad &	extrm{if distance from $u$ to the starting vertex of $P$ is $<2k$}\ \prod_{e\in R_{P}} rac{\upalpha(e)}{\upalpha_{P}(e)+\mathds{1}\{\upalpha_{P}(e)=0\}} &&	extrm{otherwise}\enspace, \end{array} ight . 
onumber \end{align} where $R_{P}$ is the path in $\deeppink{T_{P}}$ defined earlier. The above definition of ${\mathcal{N}}_A$ implies  egin{align} {\mathcal{N}}_A(P,u)\cdot {\mathcal{F}}(P, u)&= \sum
olimits_{\ell\geq 2k} \sum
olimits_{W=(e_1,\ldots, e_{\ell})\in \deeppink{T_{P}}} \prod
olimits_{1\leq i\leq \ell }\upalpha(e_{i}) \enspace, \end{align} where $W$ varies over the paths in $\deeppink{T_{P}}$ from the root to the copies of vertex $u$ at distance $\ell$ from the root. Verifying the above equality is a matter of simple calculations when $\upalpha_{P}(e)
eq 0$ for all $e\in R_{P}$. That is, it follows from \eqref{eq:FVsITs}, \eqref{eq:ProdWeigtPTPBreakNew} and the definition of ${\mathcal{N}}_A$. When there is at least one $e\in R_{P}$ such that $\upalpha_{P}(e)=0$, then it is not hard to see that we also have $\upalpha(e)=0$; hence both sides in \eqref{eq:IfVsWeightscFVsViDD} are equal to zero. All the above imply that \eqref{eq:IfVsWeightscFVsViDD} is true. Then, plugging \eqref{eq:IfVsWeightscFVsViDD} into \eqref{eq:IfVsWeightscFVsViBB}, we obtain \eqref{eq:Target4lemma:FromCalI2CalF}. Hence, we conclude that \eqref{eq:lemma:FromCalI2CalF} is true.

nodes.name: Bound $|\mathcal{N}_A|\le\max\{1,\upc^{-k}\}$
nodes.statement: The assumption that $\mu^{\Lambda,\tau}_G$ is $b$-marginally bounded implies that there is $\upc \in (0,1)$, bounded away from zero such that we either have $\upalpha_{P}(e)=0$, or $\upc\leq \abs{\upalpha_{P}(e)} \leq 1$ and similarly for $\upalpha(e)$. Hence, for any $P\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ and any vertex $u\in V\setminus \Lambda$, we have $| {\mathcal{N}}_A(P, u)| \leq \max\{1,\upc^{-k}\}$. We conclude that \Cref{lemma:FromCalI2CalF} is true for $C_A=\max\{1,\upc^{- k}\}$. \hfill $\square$

nodes.name: Reduce to the entrywise identity (18.16)
nodes.statement: In what follows, we abbreviate ${\mathcal{F}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G,k}$ and $\applegreen{{\mathcal{L}}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G,k}$ to ${\mathcal{F}}$ and $\rosegold{{\mathcal{L}}}$, respectively. Firstly, we note that the matrices at the two sides of the equation in \eqref{eq:lemma:FromCalF2CalH} are of the same dimension, i.e., they are $\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda, k}\times (V\setminus \Lambda)$. \Cref{lemma:FromCalF2CalH} follows by showing that there is an $\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda, k}\times \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ matrix ${\mathcal{N}}_B$, with entries bounded as specified in the statement of \Cref{lemma:FromCalF2CalH}, such that for any $u\in V\setminus \Lambda$ and $P\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda, k}$, we have \begin{align} {\mathcal{F}}(P, u) &= \sum\nolimits_{Q} {\mathcal{N}}_B(P, Q)\cdot \rosegold{{\mathcal{L}}}(P, Q) \enspace, \end{align} where $Q$ varies over all walks in $ \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ that emanate from vertex $u$.

nodes.name: Far pairs: reverse $\mathcal{F}$ via Claim 5.1 with factor...
nodes.statement: Consider vertices $w, u\in V\setminus \Lambda$ at distance $\geq 2k$ and $P\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ which emanates from $w$. We start by showing that for such $P$ and $w, u$, \eqref{eq:Target4lemma:FromCalF2CalH} is true. Let $\upzeta^{P}$ be the $P$-extension of $\mu^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G}$. Let ${\mathcal{I}}^{P}$ be the influence matrix induced by $\upzeta^{P}$. From \eqref{eq:SemExtIndVsInfM}, we have \begin{align} {\mathcal{F}}(P, u) &={\mathcal{I}}^{P}(w,u) ={\mathcal{W}} \cdot {\mathcal{I}}^{P}(u,w) \enspace, \end{align} where ${\mathcal{W}}={\mathcal{W}}(P, u)=\frac {\upzeta^{P}_{u}(+1)\cdot \upzeta^{P}_{u}(-1 )} {\upzeta^{P}_{w}(+1)\cdot \upzeta^{P}_{w}(-1)+\mathds{1}\{\upzeta^{P}_{w}(+1)\in \{0,1\}\}}$. To verify the second equality in \eqref{eq:CFReverse} note the following: when $\upzeta^{P}_{u}(+1), \upzeta^{P}_{w}(+1)\notin \{0,1\}$, the second equality in \eqref{eq:CFReverse} is true due to \Cref{claim:InfSymmetrisation}. When at least one of $\upzeta^{P}_{u}(1), \upzeta^{P}_{w}(1)$ is in $\{0,1\}$, the definitions of ${\mathcal{F}}$ and the influence matrix ${\mathcal{I}}^{P}$ imply ${\mathcal{F}}(P, u)=0$ and ${\mathcal{I}}^{P}(u,w)=0$. Hence, the second equality in \eqref{eq:CFReverse} is true. The $b$-marginal boundedness assumption implies \begin{align} 0\leq {\mathcal{W}}(P,u) & \leq b^{-2} \enspace. \end{align} \noindent
nodes.statement_short: Far pairs: reverse $\mathcal{F}$ via Claim 5.1 with factor $\mathcal{W}\le b^{-2}$

nodes.name: State Claim 18.3
nodes.statement: For $Q\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ that emanates from $u$, let $\upzeta^{P,Q}$ be the $\{P,Q\}$-extension of $\mu^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G}$. Note that $P$ and $Q$ are compatible because we assume that $u$ and $w$ are at distance $\geq 2k$; hence, $\upzeta^{P,Q}$ is well-defined. In what follows, denote ${\mathcal{I}}^{P,Q}$ the influence matrix induced by $\upzeta^{P,Q}$. \begin{claim} There is an $\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}\times (V\setminus \Lambda)$ matrix $\widehat{{\mathcal{N}}}_A$ such that for $w, u\in V\setminus \Lambda$ with ${\rm dist}_{G}(w,u)\geq 2k$ and any $P\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ that emanates from $w$, we have \begin{align} {\mathcal{I}}^{P}(u,w) &=\sum\nolimits_{Q} \widehat{{\mathcal{N}}}_A(Q, w) \cdot {\mathcal{I}}^{P,Q} (u,w) \enspace, \end{align} where $Q$ varies over the walks in $\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$, which emanate from $u$. Furthermore, we have \begin{align} \max\nolimits_{Q,z} \{ |\widehat{{\mathcal{N}}}_A(Q,z)| \} & \leq C_A\enspace, \end{align} where $C_A$ is specified in the statement of \Cref{lemma:FromCalI2CalF}. \end{claim}

nodes.name: Express $\mathcal{I}^P(u,w)$ through $\mathcal{L}(Q,P)$
nodes.statement: The definition of matrix $\rosegold{{\mathcal{L}}}$ and in particular \eqref{def:EdgeInflMatrixEquivalent}, imply\footnote{The definition of the $\{P,Q\}$-extension of $\mu^{\Lambda,\tau}_G$ imply that ${\mathcal{I}}^{Q,P}={\mathcal{I}}^{P,Q}$.} that, for any $P, Q\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ that emanate from the vertices $w$ and $u$, respectively, we have \begin{align} {\mathcal{I}}^{P,Q} (u, w)= \rosegold{{\mathcal{L}}}(Q,P)\enspace. \end{align} Combining \eqref{eq:CalEllAsInfluence} and \eqref{eq:CFReverseSplit}, we obtain \begin{align} {\mathcal{I}}^{P}(u,w) &= \sum\nolimits_{Q} \widehat{{\mathcal{N}}}_A(Q, w) \cdot \rosegold{{\mathcal{L}}}(Q,P)\enspace, \end{align} where recall that $Q$ varies over the walks in $\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ which emanate from $u$.

nodes.name: Reverse $\mathcal{L}(Q,P)$ with factor $\widehat{\mathcal{W}}\le...
nodes.statement: Working as in \eqref{eq:CFReverse}, we use \eqref{eq:CalEllAsInfluence} to obtain that for any $Q\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ that emanates from $u$, we have \begin{align} \rosegold{{\mathcal{L}}}(Q, P) &= \widehat{{\mathcal{W}}} \cdot \rosegold{{\mathcal{L}}}(P,Q)\enspace, \end{align} where $\widehat{{\mathcal{W}}}=\widehat{W}(P,Q)=\frac{\upzeta^{P,Q}_{w}(+1)\cdot \upzeta^{P,Q}_{w}(-1)} {\upzeta^{P,Q}_{u}(+1)\cdot \upzeta^{P,Q}_{u}(-1 )+\mathds{1}\{\upzeta^{P,Q}_{u}(+1)\in \{0,1\}\}}$. The $b$-marginal boundedness assumption implies \begin{align} 0\leq \widehat{{\mathcal{W}}}(P,Q) \leq b^{-2}\enspace. \end{align}

nodes.name: Define $\mathcal{N}_B$ and bound it
nodes.statement: We get \eqref{eq:Target4lemma:FromCalF2CalH} by plugging \eqref{eq:CFReverseSplitAA} and \eqref{eq:CHReverse} into \eqref{eq:CFReverse} while setting \begin{align} {\mathcal{N}}_B(P, Q) &={\mathcal{W}}(P,u) \cdot \widehat{{\mathcal{N}}}_A(Q,w) \cdot \widehat{{\mathcal{W}}}(P, Q)\enspace. \end{align} Recall that $u$ is the first vertex of path $Q$. Plugging \eqref{eq:Bound4CN1}, \eqref{eq:CFReverseSplitBB} and \eqref{eq:CalN2Bound} into \eqref{eq:CLVsCIPQ} we obtain that $|{\mathcal{N}}_B(P, Q)| \leq b^{-4}\cdot C_A$.

nodes.name: Close pairs: both sides vanish
nodes.statement: We consider \eqref{eq:Target4lemma:FromCalF2CalH} for $u,w\in V\setminus \Lambda$ which are at distance $< 2k$ and $P\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ that emanates from $w$. For such $u,w$ and $P$, we have \begin{align} \left(\left( \rosegold{{\mathcal{L}}} \circ {\mathcal{N}}_B \right)\cdot \UpC_{k}\right)(P,u)&=0 & \textrm{and} &&{\mathcal{F}}(P,u)&=0\enspace. \end{align} The equality on the left is true because $\left(\left( \rosegold{{\mathcal{L}}} \circ {\mathcal{N}}_B \right)\cdot \UpC_{k}\right)(P,u)= \sum_{Q} \rosegold{{\mathcal{L}}}(P,Q) \cdot {\mathcal{N}}_B(P,Q) \cdot \UpC_{k}(Q,u)$ and the variable $Q\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ varies over the walks that emanate from $u$. In this case, we have $\rosegold{{\mathcal{L}}}(P,Q)=0$ since $P$ and $Q$ are not compatible. The equality on the right follows from the definition of matrix ${\mathcal{F}}$. Hence, for any choice of matrix ${\mathcal{N}}_B$, the above is true. For matrix ${\mathcal{N}}_B$ to be well defined, for $u,w$ at distance $<2k$ and any $P, Q\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ that emanate from $w$ and $u$, respectively, we let ${\mathcal{N}}_B(P,Q)=1$. This choice of ${\mathcal{N}}_B$ and \eqref{eq:LNCVsFNonCompatiblePQ} imply that \eqref{eq:Target4lemma:FromCalF2CalH} is also true for any $u,w\in V\setminus \Lambda$ which are at distance $< 2k$ and $P$ that emanates from $w$.

nodes.name: Conclude with $C_B=\max\{1,b^{-4}C_A\}$
nodes.statement: Hence \eqref{eq:Target4lemma:FromCalF2CalH} is true for any $u,w\in V\setminus \Lambda$. We conclude that \Cref{lemma:FromCalF2CalH} is true for $C_B=\max\{1, b^{-4}\cdot C_A\}$. \hfill $\square$

nodes.name: Walk sets $\Omega,\Omega_P$ and edge sets $\mathcal{O},\mathcal{O}_P$
nodes.statement: Let $\magenta{\Omega}$ be the set of walks in $G$ which correspond to the vertices in $\applegreen{T}=T_{\rm SAW}(G,u)$. Also, let $\magenta{\Omega}_{P}$ be the set of walks in $\gext{G}{P}$ which correspond to the vertices in $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}=T_{\rm SAW}(\gext{G}{P},u)$. For concreteness, let $P=x_0, \ldots, x_{k}$. Recall that $x_0=w$ and $u\notin P$. Let set ${\mathcal{O}}$ consist of each edge $e$ in $G$ which does not connect two consecutive vertices in $P$ but has at least one end in the set of vertices $\{x_{0}, \ldots, x_{k-1}\}$. Let set ${\mathcal{O}}_{P}$ consist of the set of edges in $\gext{G}{P}$ which are between a split-vertex in set $\cadmiumgreen{\UpS}_{P}$ and another vertex of $\gext{G}{P}$. The only edges in $G$ that do not appear in $\gext{G}{P}$ are exactly those in set ${\mathcal{O}}$. Similarly, the only edges in $\gext{G}{P}$ that do not appear in $G$ are exactly those in set ${\mathcal{O}}_{P}$. Hence, the elements in $\magenta{\Omega} \cap \magenta{\Omega}_{P}$ correspond to paths that do not use edges from set ${\mathcal{O}}$ and ${\mathcal{O}}_{P}$.

nodes.name: Define the map $\upphi$
nodes.statement: We let the map $\iris{\upphi}:\magenta{\Omega}_{P}\to \magenta{\Omega}$ be defined as follows: \begin{enumerate}[(a)] \item For each $W=v_0, \ldots, v_{r}\in \magenta{\Omega}_{P}$ such that $v_{r}\notin \cadmiumgreen{\UpS}_{P}$ we set $\iris{\upphi}(W)=W$. \item For each $W=v_0, \ldots, v_{r}\in \magenta{\Omega}_{P}$ such that $v_{r}\in \cadmiumgreen{\UpS}_{P}$, we set $\iris{\upphi}(W)=W_{P}$, where $W_{P}=z_0, \ldots, z_{r}$ is such that $z_{i}=v_{i}$ for $i=0, \ldots, r-1$, while the split-vertex $v_{r}$ is generated from $z_{r}$. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Domain and codomain of $\upphi$
nodes.statement: We let the map $\iris{\upphi}:\magenta{\Omega}_{P}\to \magenta{\Omega}$ be defined as follows: \begin{enumerate}[(a)]

nodes.name: (a) walks not ending at a split-vertex
nodes.statement: For each $W=v_0, \ldots, v_{r}\in \magenta{\Omega}_{P}$ such that $v_{r}\notin \cadmiumgreen{\UpS}_{P}$ we set $\iris{\upphi}(W)=W$.
nodes.statement_short: (a) walks not ending at a split-vertex

nodes.name: (b) walks ending at a split-vertex
nodes.statement: For each $W=v_0, \ldots, v_{r}\in \magenta{\Omega}_{P}$ such that $v_{r}\in \cadmiumgreen{\UpS}_{P}$, we set $\iris{\upphi}(W)=W_{P}$, where $W_{P}=z_0, \ldots, z_{r}$ is such that $z_{i}=v_{i}$ for $i=0, \ldots, r-1$, while the split-vertex $v_{r}$ is generated from $z_{r}$. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: $\upphi$ is well defined
nodes.statement: We proceed to show that $\iris{\upphi}$ is well-defined. Since each vertex from $\cadmiumgreen{\UpS}_{P}$ is of degree one, it can only appear in a walk in $\gext{G}{P}$ as a first or as a last vertex. Hence, each $W \in \magenta{\Omega}_{P}$ such that $v_{r}\notin \cadmiumgreen{\UpS}_{P}$ does not use edges from ${\mathcal{O}}_{P}$, implying $W\in \magenta{\Omega}$. Hence, item (a) for map $\iris{\upphi}$ is well-defined. For each walk $W=v_0, \ldots, v_{r} \in \magenta{\Omega}_{P}$ such that $v_{r}\in \cadmiumgreen{\UpS}_{P}$, there is walk $W_{P}=z_0, \ldots, z_{r} \in \magenta{\Omega}$ such that $v_{i}=z_{i}$ for $i=0,\ldots, r-1$, while $z_{r}$ is a split-vertex that is generated by vertex $v_{r}$. This holds since the definition of $\gext{G}{P}$ implies that when constructing $\gext{G}{P}$, we substitute the edge $\{z_{r-1}, z_{r}\}\in {\mathcal{O}}$ with the edge $\{v_{r-1}, v_{r}\}\in {\mathcal{O}}_{P}$. Hence, item (b) for $\iris{\upphi}$ is well-defined.

nodes.name: $\upphi$ is a bijection onto its image
nodes.statement: We let $\widehat{\magenta{\Omega}} \subseteq \magenta{\Omega}$ be the image set of map $\iris{\upphi}$. The discussion in the previous paragraph implies that for each $W\in \widehat{\magenta{\Omega}}$, there is a (unique) well-defined walk $\iris{\upphi}^{-1}(W)\in \magenta{\Omega}_{P}$. Furthermore, the definition of $\widehat{\magenta{\Omega}}$ implies that $\iris{\upphi}$ is a surjective map from $\magenta{\Omega}_{P}$ to $\widehat{\magenta{\Omega}}$. We conclude that $\iris{\upphi}$ is a bijection from set $\magenta{\Omega}_{P}$ to set $\widehat{\magenta{\Omega}}$.
nodes.statement_short: $\upphi$ is a bijection onto its image

nodes.name: Lift $\upphi$ to a vertex bijection onto $\widehat T$
nodes.statement: Recalling that $\applegreen{T}=T_{\rm SAW}(G,u)$, let $\widehat{T}$ be the subtree (perhaps forest) of $\applegreen{T}$ induced by the vertices that correspond to the walks in $\widehat{\magenta{\Omega}}$. We extend the definition of $\iris{\upphi}$ and identify it as a map from the set of vertices in $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ to that in $\widehat{T}$. Particularly, $\iris{\upphi}$ is bijection between the sets of vertices of the two trees.
nodes.statement_short: Lift $\upphi$ to a vertex bijection onto $\widehat T$

nodes.name: Adjacency preservation
nodes.statement: We show that $\iris{\upphi}$ preserves adjacencies. That is, for two vertices $x$, $z$ in $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ which are adjacent, we have that $\iris{\upphi}(x)$ and $\iris{\upphi}(z)$ are two adjacent vertices in $\widehat{T}$. Suppose that $x$ and $z$ correspond to walks $W, \overline{W}\in \magenta{\Omega}_{P}$, respectively. W.l.o.g., suppose walk $ W$ extends walk $\overline{W}$ by one vertex. Then, the vertices $\iris{\upphi}(x)$ and $\iris{\upphi}(z)$ correspond to walks $\iris{\upphi}(W)$ and $\iris{\upphi}(\overline{W})$, respectively. In what follows we show that $\iris{\upphi}(W)$ extends $\iris{\upphi}(\overline{W})$. Let $\overline{W}=v_0, \ldots, v_{r}$ and $W=v_0, \ldots, v_{r+1}$. First note that we cannot have $v_{r}\in \cadmiumgreen{\UpS}_{P}$ because this would imply that walk $\overline{W}$ cannot be extended as $v_{r}$ is of degree 1. Hence we always have $v_{r}\notin \cadmiumgreen{\UpS}_{P}$. We consider cases for $v_{r+1}$. If $v_{r+1}\notin \cadmiumgreen{\UpS}_{P}$, then we have $\iris{\upphi}(\overline{W})=\overline{W}$ and $\iris{\upphi}(W)=W$. Clearly, in this case, $\iris{\upphi}(W)$ extends path $\iris{\upphi}(\overline{W})$. If $ v_{r+1}\in \cadmiumgreen{\UpS}_{P}$, then we have $\iris{\upphi}(W)=W_{P}$, where $W_{P}=z_0, \ldots, z_{r+1}$ is such that $z_{i}=v_{i}$ for $i=0, \ldots, r$, while the split-vertex $v_{r+1}$ is generated from $z_{r+1}$. Clearly we have that $W_{P}$ extends walk $\overline{W}$. The above implies that $\iris{\upphi}(W)$ extends $\iris{\upphi}(\overline{W})$. The conclusion of the previous paragraph implies that $\iris{\upphi}(x)$ and $\iris{\upphi}(z)$ are two adjacent vertices in $\widehat{T}$. Hence, $\iris{\upphi}$ preserves adjacencies between the two trees $\widehat{T}$ and $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$.

nodes.name: Restate adjacency preservation
nodes.statement: That is, for two vertices $x$, $z$ in $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ which are adjacent, we have that $\iris{\upphi}(x)$ and $\iris{\upphi}(z)$ are two adjacent vertices in $\widehat{T}$.

nodes.name: Take an extending pair of walks
nodes.statement: Suppose that $x$ and $z$ correspond to walks $W, \overline{W}\in \magenta{\Omega}_{P}$, respectively. W.l.o.g., suppose walk $ W$ extends walk $\overline{W}$ by one vertex. Then, the vertices $\iris{\upphi}(x)$ and $\iris{\upphi}(z)$ correspond to walks $\iris{\upphi}(W)$ and $\iris{\upphi}(\overline{W})$, respectively. In what follows we show that $\iris{\upphi}(W)$ extends $\iris{\upphi}(\overline{W})$.
nodes.statement_short: Take an extending pair of walks

nodes.name: Case analysis on the last vertex
nodes.statement: Let $\overline{W}=v_0, \ldots, v_{r}$ and $W=v_0, \ldots, v_{r+1}$. First note that we cannot have $v_{r}\in \cadmiumgreen{\UpS}_{P}$ because this would imply that walk $\overline{W}$ cannot be extended as $v_{r}$ is of degree 1. Hence we always have $v_{r}\notin \cadmiumgreen{\UpS}_{P}$. We consider cases for $v_{r+1}$. If $v_{r+1}\notin \cadmiumgreen{\UpS}_{P}$, then we have $\iris{\upphi}(\overline{W})=\overline{W}$ and $\iris{\upphi}(W)=W$. Clearly, in this case, $\iris{\upphi}(W)$ extends path $\iris{\upphi}(\overline{W})$. If $ v_{r+1}\in \cadmiumgreen{\UpS}_{P}$, then we have $\iris{\upphi}(W)=W_{P}$, where $W_{P}=z_0, \ldots, z_{r+1}$ is such that $z_{i}=v_{i}$ for $i=0, \ldots, r$, while the split-vertex $v_{r+1}$ is generated from $z_{r+1}$. Clearly we have that $W_{P}$ extends walk $\overline{W}$. The above implies that $\iris{\upphi}(W)$ extends $\iris{\upphi}(\overline{W})$.
nodes.statement_short: Case analysis on the last vertex

nodes.name: Adjacency is preserved
nodes.statement: The conclusion of the previous paragraph implies that $\iris{\upphi}(x)$ and $\iris{\upphi}(z)$ are two adjacent vertices in $\widehat{T}$. Hence, $\iris{\upphi}$ preserves adjacencies between the two trees $\widehat{T}$ and $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$.

nodes.name: $\upphi$ respects copies
nodes.statement: The definition of $\iris{\upphi}$ also implies the following: if vertex $v$ in $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ is a copy of vertex $\overline{v}$ in $\gext{G}{P}$ and $\overline{v}$ is not a split-vertex, then $\iris{\upphi}(v)$ is also a copy of $\overline{v}$. If $v$ is a copy of the split-vertex which is generated by vertex $\overline{v} \in P$, then $\iris{\upphi}(v)$ is a copy of $\overline{v}$.

nodes.name: $\overline T$ is a subtree of $T$ with the same root
nodes.statement: All the above imply that we can identify $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ with the tree $\widehat{T}$. Consequently, we can identify $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ as a subtree of $\applegreen{T}$. The two trees $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ and $\applegreen{T}$ have the same root, since they both consider the walks starting from vertex $u$.
nodes.statement_short: $\overline T$ is a subtree of $T$ with the same root

nodes.name: Remaining vertices descend from copies of $P$
nodes.statement: We now consider the set of vertices $v$ in $\applegreen{T}\setminus \overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$. The vertiex $v $corresponda to a walk $W\in \magenta{\Omega}\setminus \widehat{\magenta{\Omega}}$. Recall that we set $P=x_0, \ldots, x_{k}$. Then, for walk $W=v_0, \ldots, v_{r}\in \magenta{\Omega}\setminus \widehat{\magenta{\Omega}}$ there exists $j<r$ such that $v_{j}$ is a copy of a vertex in $P \setminus\{ x_{k}\}$ while $v_{j+1}$ is a copy of a vertex outside $P$. This implies that vertex $v$ in $\applegreen{T}$ is a descendant of a copy of $v_{j}$ in $\byzantine{{\tt A}}_{P}$. Recall that set $\byzantine{{\tt A}}_{P}$ consist of each vertex in $\applegreen{T}$ which is a copy of a vertex in $P$. All the above conclude the proof of \Cref{lemma:Subtree4TSawU}. \hfill $\square$
nodes.statement_short: Remaining vertices descend from copies of $P$

nodes.name: Recall the setting of Lemma 8.3
nodes.statement: The setting in this proof is the same as in the proof of \Cref{lemma:Subtree4TSawU}. Recall that we have vertices $w,u$ in graph $G$ such that ${\rm dist}_{G}(u,w)\geq 2k$ and a self-avoiding path $P$ of length $k$ that emanates from vertex $w$; hence, we have $u\notin P$.

nodes.name: Recall the map $\upphi$
nodes.statement: Let $\magenta{\Omega}$ be the set of walks in $G$ which correspond to the vertices in $\applegreen{T}=T_{\rm SAW}(G,u)$. Also, let $\magenta{\Omega}_{P}$ be the set of walks in $\gext{G}{P}$ which correspond to the vertices in $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}=T_{\rm SAW}(\gext{G}{P},u)$. We use the same map $\iris{\upphi}:\magenta{\Omega}_{P}\to \magenta{\Omega}$ as in the proof of \Cref{lemma:Subtree4TSawU}. That is, \begin{enumerate}[(a)] \item For each $W=v_0, \ldots, v_{r}\in \magenta{\Omega}_{P}$ such that $v_{r}\notin \cadmiumgreen{\UpS}_{P}$ we set $\iris{\upphi}(W)=W$. \item For each $W=v_0, \ldots, v_{r}\in \magenta{\Omega}_{P}$ such that $v_{r}\in \cadmiumgreen{\UpS}_{P}$, we set $\iris{\upphi}(W)=W_{P}$, where $W_{P}=z_0, \ldots, z_{r}$ is such that $z_{i}=v_{i}$ for $i=0, \ldots, r-1$, while the split-vertex $v_{r}$ is generated from $z_{r}$. \end{enumerate} We let $\widehat{\magenta{\Omega}} \subseteq \magenta{\Omega}$ be the image set of $\iris{\upphi}$. Let $\widehat{T}$ be the subtree of $\applegreen{T}$ induced by the vertices that correspond to the walks in $\widehat{\magenta{\Omega}}$. We showed in the proof of \Cref{lemma:Subtree4TSawU} that we can identify $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ as a subtree of $\applegreen{T}$, in particular, we identify $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ as the subtree $\widehat{T}$ of $\applegreen{T}$, using $\iris{\upphi}$. Every vertex in $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ corresponds to two walks, one walk in $\gext{G}{P}$ and another in $G$, e.g., the walk $W\in \magenta{\Omega}_{P}$ and the walk $\iris{\upphi}(W)\in \widehat{\magenta{\Omega}}\subseteq \magenta{\Omega}$.

nodes.name: Walk sets $\Omega,\Omega_P$
nodes.statement: Let $\magenta{\Omega}$ be the set of walks in $G$ which correspond to the vertices in $\applegreen{T}=T_{\rm SAW}(G,u)$. Also, let $\magenta{\Omega}_{P}$ be the set of walks in $\gext{G}{P}$ which correspond to the vertices in $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}=T_{\rm SAW}(\gext{G}{P},u)$. We use the same map $\iris{\upphi}:\magenta{\Omega}_{P}\to \magenta{\Omega}$ as in the proof of \Cref{lemma:Subtree4TSawU}. That is, \begin{enumerate}[(a)]

nodes.name: (a) of the map
nodes.statement: For each $W=v_0, \ldots, v_{r}\in \magenta{\Omega}_{P}$ such that $v_{r}\notin \cadmiumgreen{\UpS}_{P}$ we set $\iris{\upphi}(W)=W$.

nodes.name: (b) of the map
nodes.statement: For each $W=v_0, \ldots, v_{r}\in \magenta{\Omega}_{P}$ such that $v_{r}\in \cadmiumgreen{\UpS}_{P}$, we set $\iris{\upphi}(W)=W_{P}$, where $W_{P}=z_0, \ldots, z_{r}$ is such that $z_{i}=v_{i}$ for $i=0, \ldots, r-1$, while the split-vertex $v_{r}$ is generated from $z_{r}$. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Recall the identification of $\overline T$ with $\widehat T$
nodes.statement: We let $\widehat{\magenta{\Omega}} \subseteq \magenta{\Omega}$ be the image set of $\iris{\upphi}$. Let $\widehat{T}$ be the subtree of $\applegreen{T}$ induced by the vertices that correspond to the walks in $\widehat{\magenta{\Omega}}$. We showed in the proof of \Cref{lemma:Subtree4TSawU} that we can identify $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ as a subtree of $\applegreen{T}$, in particular, we identify $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ as the subtree $\widehat{T}$ of $\applegreen{T}$, using $\iris{\upphi}$. Every vertex in $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ corresponds to two walks, one walk in $\gext{G}{P}$ and another in $G$, e.g., the walk $W\in \magenta{\Omega}_{P}$ and the walk $\iris{\upphi}(W)\in \widehat{\magenta{\Omega}}\subseteq \magenta{\Omega}$.
nodes.statement_short: Recall the identification of $\overline T$ with $\widehat T$

nodes.name: Walk classes behind the pinned set $M$
nodes.statement: Furthermore, we apply the $T_{\rm SAW}$-construction on $\mu^{\Lambda,\tau}_G$ and obtain the Gibbs distribution $\mu^{M,\sigma}_{\applegreen{T}}$ for tree $\applegreen{T}=T_{\rm SAW}(G,u)$. We proceed to identify the walks in $\magenta{\Omega}$ that correspond to the vertices in $M$. Specifically, consider the following subsets of $\magenta{\Omega}$, \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item set $\magenta{\Omega}^{\Lambda}\subseteq \magenta{\Omega}$ consists of all self-avoiding walks whose last vertex is in $\Lambda$, \item set $\magenta{\Omega}^{(b)}\subseteq \magenta{\Omega}$ consists of all walks $W=v_0, \ldots, v_{r} \in \magenta{\Omega}$ such that $v_0, \ldots, v_{r-1}$ is self-avoiding and $v_{r}$ repeats, while $W\cap P\neq \emptyset$, \item set $\magenta{\Omega}^{(c)}\subseteq \magenta{\Omega}$ consists of all walks $W=v_0, \ldots, v_{r} \in \magenta{\Omega}$ such that $v_0, \ldots, v_{r-1}$ is self-avoiding and $v_{r}$ repeats, while $W\cap P= \emptyset$. \end{enumerate} The $T_{\rm SAW}$-construction implies that set $M$ consists of the vertices that correspond to the walks in the three aforementioned categories.
nodes.statement_short: Walk classes behind the pinned set $M$

nodes.name: Pinned set $M$ of $\mu^{M,\sigma}_T$
nodes.statement: Furthermore, we apply the $T_{\rm SAW}$-construction on $\mu^{\Lambda,\tau}_G$ and obtain the Gibbs distribution $\mu^{M,\sigma}_{\applegreen{T}}$ for tree $\applegreen{T}=T_{\rm SAW}(G,u)$. We proceed to identify the walks in $\magenta{\Omega}$ that correspond to the vertices in $M$. Specifically, consider the following subsets of $\magenta{\Omega}$, \begin{enumerate}[(i)]

nodes.name: (i) $\Omega^\Lambda$
nodes.statement: set $\magenta{\Omega}^{\Lambda}\subseteq \magenta{\Omega}$ consists of all self-avoiding walks whose last vertex is in $\Lambda$,

nodes.name: (ii) $\Omega^{(b)}$
nodes.statement: set $\magenta{\Omega}^{(b)}\subseteq \magenta{\Omega}$ consists of all walks $W=v_0, \ldots, v_{r} \in \magenta{\Omega}$ such that $v_0, \ldots, v_{r-1}$ is self-avoiding and $v_{r}$ repeats, while $W\cap P\neq \emptyset$,

nodes.name: (iii) $\Omega^{(c)}$
nodes.statement: set $\magenta{\Omega}^{(c)}\subseteq \magenta{\Omega}$ consists of all walks $W=v_0, \ldots, v_{r} \in \magenta{\Omega}$ such that $v_0, \ldots, v_{r-1}$ is self-avoiding and $v_{r}$ repeats, while $W\cap P= \emptyset$. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: $M$ corresponds to these walks
nodes.statement: The $T_{\rm SAW}$-construction implies that set $M$ consists of the vertices that correspond to the walks in the three aforementioned categories.

nodes.name: Walk classes behind the pinned set $L$
nodes.statement: Also, we use the $T_{\rm SAW}$-construction for the $P$-extension of $\mu^{\Lambda,\tau}_G$ and get the Gibbs distribution $\mu^{L,\eta}_{\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}}$ for tree $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}=T_{\rm SAW}(\gext{G}{P},u)$. We proceed to identify the walks in $\magenta{\Omega}_{P}$ that correspond to the vertices in $L$. Consider the following subsets of $\magenta{\Omega}_{P}$, \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \setcounter{enumi}{3} \item set $\magenta{\Omega}^{\Lambda}_{P}\subseteq \magenta{\Omega}_{P}$ consist of all self-avoiding walks whose last vertex is in $\Lambda$, \item set $\magenta{\Omega}^{(b)}_{P}\subseteq \magenta{\Omega}_{P}$ consists of all self-avoiding walks whose last vertex is in $\cadmiumgreen{\UpS}_{P}$, \item set $\magenta{\Omega}^{(c)}_{P}\subseteq \magenta{\Omega}_{P}$ consists of all walks $W=v_0, \ldots, v_{r} \in \magenta{\Omega}$ such that $v_0, \ldots, v_{r-1}$ is self-avoiding and $v_{r}$ repeats, while $W\cap P\neq \emptyset$. \end{enumerate} It is not hard to verify that set $L$ consists of the vertices that correspond to the walks of the above three categories.
nodes.statement_short: Walk classes behind the pinned set $L$

nodes.name: Pinned set $L$ of $\mu^{L,\eta}_{\overline T}$
nodes.statement: Also, we use the $T_{\rm SAW}$-construction for the $P$-extension of $\mu^{\Lambda,\tau}_G$ and get the Gibbs distribution $\mu^{L,\eta}_{\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}}$ for tree $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}=T_{\rm SAW}(\gext{G}{P},u)$. We proceed to identify the walks in $\magenta{\Omega}_{P}$ that correspond to the vertices in $L$. Consider the following subsets of $\magenta{\Omega}_{P}$, \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \setcounter{enumi}{3}

nodes.name: (iv) $\Omega^\Lambda_P$
nodes.statement: set $\magenta{\Omega}^{\Lambda}_{P}\subseteq \magenta{\Omega}_{P}$ consist of all self-avoiding walks whose last vertex is in $\Lambda$,

nodes.name: (v) $\Omega^{(b)}_P$
nodes.statement: set $\magenta{\Omega}^{(b)}_{P}\subseteq \magenta{\Omega}_{P}$ consists of all self-avoiding walks whose last vertex is in $\cadmiumgreen{\UpS}_{P}$,

nodes.name: (vi) $\Omega^{(c)}_P$
nodes.statement: set $\magenta{\Omega}^{(c)}_{P}\subseteq \magenta{\Omega}_{P}$ consists of all walks $W=v_0, \ldots, v_{r} \in \magenta{\Omega}$ such that $v_0, \ldots, v_{r-1}$ is self-avoiding and $v_{r}$ repeats, while $W\cap P\neq \emptyset$. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: $L$ corresponds to these walks
nodes.statement: It is not hard to verify that set $L$ consists of the vertices that correspond to the walks of the above three categories.

nodes.name: Prove (a)-(d) in turn
nodes.statement: We use all the above to prove statements \ref{statement:lemma:BoundaryTVsBoundaryTPFromUA}-\ref{statement:lemma:BoundaryTVsBoundaryTPFromUD} of \Cref{lemma:BoundaryTVsBoundaryTPFromU}.

nodes.name: Statement (a): pinnings agree on $L\cap M$
nodes.statement: We start with statement \ref{statement:lemma:BoundaryTVsBoundaryTPFromUA}. For each vertex $v\in M\cap L$, there are two alternatives. In the first one, vertex $v$ corresponds to a walk $W\in \magenta{\Omega}^{\Lambda}_{P}$ and $\iris{\upphi}(W)\in \magenta{\Omega}^{\Lambda}$. In the second alternative, vertex $v$ corresponds to a walk $W\in \magenta{\Omega}^{(c)}_{P}$ and $\iris{\upphi}(W)\in \magenta{\Omega}^{(c)}$. To see the above, note that for each walk $W\in \magenta{\Omega}^{\Lambda}_{P}\cup\magenta{\Omega}^{(c)}_{P}$, the definition of $\iris{\upphi}$ implies that we should have $\iris{\upphi}(W)\in \magenta{\Omega}^{\Lambda}\cup \magenta{\Omega}^{(c)}$. On the other hand, for each walk $W\in \magenta{\Omega}^{(b)}_{P}$ we have $\iris{\upphi}(W)\notin (\magenta{\Omega}^{\Lambda}\cup \magenta{\Omega}^{(b)} \cup\magenta{\Omega}^{(c)})$. This is because $\iris{\upphi}(W)$ is a self-avoiding walk in $G$ from $u$ to a vertex in $P$. Hence, every vertex $v$ which corresponds to walk $W\in \magenta{\Omega}^{(b)}_{P}$ does not belong to $M$. Also, for every $W\in \magenta{\Omega}^{(b)}$, we have that $\iris{\upphi}^{-1}(W)$ is not defined, implying that the vertex $v$ which corresponds to walk $W$ does not belong to $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$; hence it does not belong to $L$. Statement \ref{statement:lemma:BoundaryTVsBoundaryTPFromUA} follows by noting that the definition of the $T_{\rm SAW}$-construction implies that all vertices in $M\cap L$ take on the same pinning, i.e., there are no copies of split-vertices in this intersection.

nodes.name: Statement (b): $A_P\cap\overline T=\overline A_P$
nodes.statement: As far as statement \ref{statement:lemma:BoundaryTVsBoundaryTPFromUB} is concerned, note that each vertex $v\in \byzantine{{\tt A}}_{P} \cap \overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ can only correspond to a self-avoiding walk $W\in \magenta{\Omega}$ which ends at a vertex in $P$. The definition of $\iris{\upphi}$ implies that $\iris{\upphi}^{-1}(W)$ is well-defined and corresponds to a self-avoiding walk in $\magenta{\Omega}_{P}$ whose last vertex is either in $P$ or in $\cadmiumgreen{\UpS}_{P}$. Hence, it follows from the definition of set $\magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$ that $v\in \magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$. This proves \ref{statement:lemma:BoundaryTVsBoundaryTPFromUB}.

nodes.name: Statement (c): $L\setminus M\subseteq A_P$ and $M\cap\overline...
nodes.statement: We proceed to prove statement \ref{stat:C-lemma:BoundaryTVsBoundaryTPFromU}. The previous discussion shows that each vertex $v\in L\setminus M$ corresponds to a walk $W\in \magenta{\Omega}^{(b)}_{P}$. Furthermore, the definition of $\iris{\upphi}$ implies that the last vertex of walk $\iris{\upphi}(W)$ is in $P$. Hence, we have $v\in \byzantine{{\tt A}}_{P}$. We conclude that $L\setminus M\subseteq \byzantine{{\tt A}}_{P}$. If vertex $v\in M\cap \overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ corresponds to a walk $W\in \magenta{\Omega}^{\Lambda}$, then the definition of $\iris{\upphi}$ implies that $\iris{\upphi}^{-1}(W)\in \magenta{\Omega}^{\Lambda}_{P}$; hence $v\in L$. Similarly, if vertex $v\in M\cap \overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ corresponds to a walk $W\in \magenta{\Omega}^{(c)}$, then it also corresponds to walk $\iris{\upphi}^{-1}(W)\in \magenta{\Omega}^{(c)}_{P}$; hence $v\in L$. We conclude that $M\cap \overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}\subseteq L$ by noting that there is no vertex $v\in M\cap \overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ which corresponds to a walk $W\in \magenta{\Omega}^{(b)}$ (this was also noted in the proof of \ref{statement:lemma:BoundaryTVsBoundaryTPFromUA}). The two conclusions that $L\setminus M\subseteq \byzantine{{\tt A}}_{P}$ and that $M\cap \overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}\subseteq L$ imply that statement \ref{stat:C-lemma:BoundaryTVsBoundaryTPFromU} is true.
nodes.statement_short: Statement (c): $L\setminus M\subseteq A_P$ and $M\cap\overline T\subseteq L$

nodes.name: Statement (d): pinning $A_P$ screens off the rest of $T$
nodes.statement: We proceed to prove statement \ref{statement:lemma:BoundaryTVsBoundaryTPFromUD}. This follows directly by recalling that all vertices in $T\setminus \overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ are descendants of the vertices in $\byzantine{{\tt A}}_{P}$. Hence, after pinning the vertices in $L\cup \byzantine{{\tt A}}_{P}$, the vertices in $T\setminus \overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ have no effect on the configurations of the vertices in $T\cap \overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$. All the above conclude the proof of \Cref{lemma:BoundaryTVsBoundaryTPFromU}. \hfill $\square$
nodes.statement_short: Statement (d): pinning $A_P$ screens off the rest of $T$

nodes.name: State Claims 19.1 and 19.2

nodes.name: Choose a random vertex
nodes.statement: Choose uniformly at random a vertex $v\in V$.

nodes.name: Copy the other spins
nodes.statement: For every vertex $w$ different than $v$, set $X_{t+1}(w)=X_{t}(w)$.

nodes.name: Heat-bath update at $v$
nodes.statement: Set $X_{t+1}(v)$ according to the marginal of $\mu$ at $v$, conditional on the neighbours of $v$ having the configuration specified by $X_{t+1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Resample the spin at $v$ from its conditional marginal
